jobs.description:
Job Family

Underwriting

About Us

At Transamerica, hard work, innovative thinking, and personal accountability are qualities we honor and reward. We understand the potential of leveraging the talents of a diverse workforce. We embrace an environment where employees enjoy a balance between their careers, families, communities, and personal interests.

Ultimately, we appreciate the uniqueness of a company where talented professionals work collaboratively in a positive environment — one focused on helping people look forward and plan for the best life possible while providing tools and solutions that make it easier to get there.

   

Who We Are

 

We believe everyone deserves to live their best life. More than a century ago, we were among the first financial services companies in America to serve everyday people from all walks of life.

Today, we’re part of an international holding company, with millions of customers and thousands of employees worldwide. Our insurance, retirement, and investment solutions help people make the most of what’s important to them.

We’re empowered by a vast agent network covering North America, with diversity to match. Together with our nonprofit research institute and foundation, we tune in, step up, and are a force for good — for our customers and the communities where we live, work, and play. United in our purpose, we help people create the financial freedom to live life on their terms.

What We Do

Transamerica is organized into three distinct businesses. These include 1) World Financial Group, including Transamerica Financial Advisors, 2) Protection Solutions and Savings & Investments, comprised of life insurance, annuities, employee benefits, retirement plans, and Transamerica Investment Solutions, and 3) Financial Assets, which includes legacy blocks of long term care, universal life, and variable and fixed annuities. These are supported by Transamerica Corporate, which includes Finance, People and Places, General Counsel, Risk, Internal Audit, Strategy and Development, and Corporate Affairs, which covers Communications, Brand, and Government and Policy Affairs.

Transamerica employs nearly 7,000 people. It’s part of Aegon, an integrated, diversified, international financial services group servingapproximately 23.9 million customersworldwide.* For more information, visit transamerica.com. 

Job Description Summary

Design, deliver, and administer specialized training in life, annuity, and health underwriting covering analysis techniques, risk assessment, modeling, and tools and technology used to interpret and apply criteria for accurate risk assessments. Implement career development and engagement programs to improve the employee experience.

Job Description

Responsibilities

  • Apply best practices in curriculum design and delivery to department staff and stakeholders in alignment with industry and company requirements.
  • Develop clear and measurable learning criteria for different levels of underwriting knowledge and technical expertise.
  • Keep current on regulatory rules, product offerings, and technology advances. Share insights through group and individual training.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of training/identify gaps and collaborate with management on ways to enhance the learning experience.
  • Assess team needs to identify and create opportunities for career development and employee engagement.
  • Participate in cross-functional projects/programs requiring collaboration with Underwriting.

Qualifications

  • Six years of underwriting experience in the insurance/financial services industry
  • Skilled in underwriting training or project/process management in a corporate environment
  • Outstanding written and oral communication and presentation skills
  • Ability to communicate technical information in a learning environment
  • Strong documentation and writing/editing skills
  • Creative thinker and collaborator to design engaging learning and development programs
  • Proficiency using MS Office

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in business or finance
  • FLMI, FALU, or CLU certification

Working Conditions

  • Remote Environment

The Salary for this position generally ranges between $90,000-105,000 annually. Please note that the salary range is a good faith estimate for this position and actual starting pay is determined by several factors including qualifications, experience, geography, work location designation (in-office, hybrid, remote) and operational needs. Salary may vary above and below the stated amounts, as permitted by applicable law.


Additionally, this position is typically eligible for an Annual Bonus of 12.5% based on the Company Bonus Plan/Individual Performance and is at the Company’s discretion.


Disclaimer:

  • We will never request personal information such as ID or payment for equipment upfront.
  • Official offers are sent via DocuSign following a verbal offer—not through text or email

This job description is not a contract of employment nor for any specific job responsibilities. The Company may change, add to, remove, or revoke the terms of this job description at its discretion. Managers may assign other duties and responsibilities as needed. In the event an employee or applicant requests or requires an accommodation to perform job functions, the applicable HR Business Partner should be contacted to evaluate the accommodation request.

What We Offer

For eligible employees, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support both the personal and financial well-being of our employees.

Compensation Benefits

  • Competitive Pay

  • Bonus for Eligible Employees

Benefits Package

  • Pension Plan

  • 401k Match

  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan

  • Tuition Reimbursement

  • Disability Insurance

  • Medical Insurance

  • Dental Insurance

  • Vision Insurance

  • Employee Discounts

  • Career Training & Development Opportunities

Health and Work/Life Balance Benefits

  • Paid Time Off starting at 160 hours annually for employees in their first year of service.

  • Ten (10) paid holidays per year (typically mirroring the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) holidays).

  • Be Well Company holistic wellness program, which includes Wellness Coaching and Reward Dollars

  • Parental Leave – fifteen (15) days of paid parental leave per calendar year to eligible employees with at least one year of service at the time of birth, placement of an adopted child, or placement of a foster care child.

  • Adoption Assistance

  • Employee Assistance Program

  • Back-Up Care Program

  • PTO for Volunteer Hours

  • Employee Matching Gifts Program

  • Employee Resource Groups

  • Inclusion and Diversity Programs

  • Employee Recognition Program

  • Referral Bonus Programs

Inclusion & Diversity 

 

We believe our commitment to diversity and inclusion creates a work environment filled with exceptional individuals. We’re thrilled to have been recognized for our efforts through the Human Rights Campaign Corporate Equality Index, Dave Thomas Adoption Friendly Advocate, and several Seramount lists, including the Inclusion Index, 100 Best Companies for Working Parents, Best Companies for Dads, and Top 75 Companies for Executive Women.

 

To foster a culture of inclusivity throughout our workforce, workplace, and marketplace, Transamerica offers a wide range of diversity and inclusion programs. This includes our company-sponsored, employee-driven Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), which are formed around a shared interest or a common characteristic of diversity. ERGs are open to all employees. They provide a supportive environment to help us better appreciate our similarities and differences and understand how they benefit us all.

  

Giving Back 

 

We believe our responsibilities extend beyond our corporate walls. That's why we created the Aegon Transamerica Foundation in 1994. Through a mix of financial grants and the volunteer efforts of our employees, the foundation supports nonprofit organizations focused on the things that matter most to our people in the communities where we live and work.   

 

Transamerica’s Parent Company 

Aegon acquired the Transamerica business in 1999. Since its start in 1844, Aegon has grown into an international company serving more than 23.9 million people across the globe.* It offers investment, protection, and retirement solutions, always with a clear purpose: Helping people live their best lives. As a leading global investor and employer, the company seeks to have a positive impact by addressing critical environmental and societal issues, with a focus on climate change and inclusion and diversity.  

* As of December 31, 2023

Revenue, Technical Accounting & Policy Senior Manager


POSITION OVERVIEW

MRI Software is seeking a Revenue, Technical Accounting & Policy Senior Manager to lead a newly established global team responsible for revenue recognition, technical accounting and accounting policy. The role will provide authoritative accounting guidance, establish and maintain group-wide accounting policies, govern significant revenue accounting judgements and support complex commercial arrangements, financial reporting and the overall control environment.


ROLE & RESPONSIBILITIES


Revenue recognition governance:

  • Lead the accounting review of material, unusual and non-standard customer arrangements to ensure appropriate revenue recognition outcomes.
  • Own and maintain the revenue recognition framework across all revenue types (eg. SaaS, subscription, term licence, perpetual licence, maintenance, implementation, professional services, usage-based and partner arrangements).
  • Review and challenge the conclusions of the revenue accounting team, ensuring revenue is recognised appropriately and that process, system or control gaps are identified and remediated in partnership with the Finance Transformation team.
  • Approve revenue accounting adjustments arising from contract reviews, accounting assessments or control activities.
  • Partner with Sales and Legal teams to ensure the optimal revenue outcome from in-flight contracts.

Technical accounting and policy:

  • Own the group accounting policy manual and ensure policies remain current, practical and consistently applied across regions.
  • Research complex accounting matters and provide clear and practical guidance to stakeholders across the business.
  • Act as the accounting subject matter expert for significant accounting judgements impacting statutory and group reporting.
  • Prepare and review audit-ready technical accounting papers that clearly articulate the relevant facts, accounting guidance, analysis, judgements and conclusions.
  • Monitor new accounting standards and regulatory developments; assess impact and lead on adoption.

Other:

  • Partner with the Audit, Controls & Reporting Manager to:

odesign and maintain key controls.

osupport the successful delivery of statutory and group audits.

  • Partner with Legal, Commercial and Corporate Development teams to provide accounting guidance on significant customer arrangements, strategic transactions and acquisitions.
  • Develop the capability of the wider finance organisation through training, guidance and coaching.
  • Drive simplification, standardisation and automation while preserving appropriate review and control.

REQUIREMENTS

jobs.description:
At Sword, we’re building AI to heal billions and unlock humanity’s full potential. In doing so, we’re pioneering AI Care, a fundamentally new approach to healthcare built for medical reasoning, safety, and real-time treatment, not generic technology applied after the fact. As both a clinical-centric frontier AI lab and an applied AI platform, Sword is reimagining how care is delivered at scale, removing traditional barriers like appointments, waiting rooms, and stigma so more people can access the care they need—and ultimately get back to lives lived in full.

Since 2020, Sword has expanded across physical therapy, women’s health, cardiometabolic, and mental health, and is now moving beyond the session to a fully AI-native, 24/7 care program that brings physical activity, therapeutic exercise, psychotherapy, nutrition, and behavior change into one connected experience. More than 700,000 members across three continents have completed over 10 million AI sessions, helping 1,000+ enterprise clients avoid more than $1 billion in unnecessary healthcare costs. Backed by 42 clinical studies, 44+ patents, and more than $500 million raised from leading investors including Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, and Founders Fund, Sword is defining a new standard for healthcare.

AI Proficiency at Sword

AI fluency is a core expectation at Sword. Every candidate is assessed against our three-level framework — be ready to share real examples of how AI is already part of how you work.

  • Explorer (Level 1) — Uses AI daily to boost personal productivity

  • Builder (Level 2) — Creates workflows and tools that elevate the whole team

  • Integrator (Level 3) — Embeds AI into products and processes at scale

Every hire must demonstrate at least Level 1. The expected level will vary depending on the seniority of the role.

Role

Headspace reaches millions of members through 1,500+ employer and health plan clients. As CRM Lead, you'll set the B2B2C lifecycle strategy with the leadership and personally deliver it for a focused portfolio of utilization-based and strategic accounts, where CRM performance directly affects contract outcomes. You'll also build the foundation that lets the rest of the book run at scale, and you'll lead and develop the CRM Manager.

This is a true player-coach role. Expect to spend roughly half your time building in Braze and the rest on strategy, architecture, experimentation, and coaching.

What you’ll be doing

  • Define the B2B2C CRM strategy and roadmap in collaboration with leadership, covering activation, engagement, and retention
  • Own CRM execution for utilization-based and strategic accounts: design, build, QA, launch, and optimize custom journeys in Braze
  • Track member utilization and engagement against contractual targets, and adjust programs to close gaps
  • Partner with Client Success and account teams to tailor programs to client population, goals, and commitments at scale
  • Build the foundational infrastructure for the scaled book, including base Canvas architecture, client-level segmentation, and dynamic content frameworks, so the Manager can operate it at volume
  • Own the data and segmentation architecture, including custom attributes and events and how org-level context drives personalization
  • Run the experimentation program: hypotheses, test design, readouts, and roadmap decisions
  • Pilot new approaches with priority accounts, then hand proven plays to the Manager to scale across the book
  • Set standards for Canvas architecture, naming conventions, and measurement
  • Manage, coach, and develop the CRM Manager: set priorities, give feedback, and decide when requests from the broader book warrant custom work
  • Own the performance narrative for senior leadership
  • Coordinate with Product, Data/Analytics, Legal/Compliance, and the D2C CRM team

What you need to have

  • 7+ years in CRM or lifecycle marketing with deep, hands-on Braze expertise (Canvas, Liquid, Connected Content, segmentation, event-driven triggers)
  • A record of defining strategy and personally building and shipping it
  • Experience managing a small portfolio of performance-linked accounts where CRM outcomes affect contract results
  • Experience managing or mentoring others, formally or informally
  • Comfort with SQL and analytics tools (Snowflake, Amplitude), and the ability to turn data into decisions
  • Strong presence with senior stakeholders and cross-functional influence
  • Experience with B2B2C, benefits, or health-adjacent products (preferred)
  • Familiarity with HIPAA and privacy-conscious data practices (preferred)

How success is measured

  • Utilization and engagement outcomes for utilization-based and strategic accounts
  • A clear, adopted roadmap
  • A sound, scalable Braze architecture that the Manager can run
  • Proven plays that get successfully scaled
  • The growth and effectiveness of your direct report

This is a starting point, not a ceiling — once someone joins and proves they're outlier talent, we adjust quickly to make sure their compensation matches their impact.

In this dynamic role, you will be the captain of your own ship, taking true end-to-end ownership of managing, processing, and reconciling multi-country payrolls using modern tools and systems.

Supported by accessible leadership and a highly collaborative culture, you will tackle complex challenges while ensuring strict adherence to local statutory compliance, tax laws, and internal controls. Serving as a trusted advisor to cross-functional partners, you’ll leverage your individual agility to drive continuous growth, seamless operational delivery, and exceptional employee support across the region.

What You'll Do

    • Audit, validate, and reconcile complex payroll data against source files, ensuring complete accuracy and compliance before final approval
    • Advise and align with internal stakeholders (HR, Finance, and Employee Success) and external service providers to deliver expert advisory support on complex compliance and payroll matters, ensuring data accuracy and proper employee classification
    • Master and implement evolving EU payroll tax regulations, proactively safeguarding regional compliance standards and mitigating risk
    • Spearhead process improvement initiatives, architecting new workflows and driving successful regional adoption

    • 7+ years of professional payroll experience in a fast-paced, multi-national environment handling EMEA payroll
    • Strong knowledge of EU payroll tax regulations, social contributions, and statutory compliance requirements
    • High attention to detail, proactive problem-solving, fast-learning ability, and a collaborative, customer-first approach
    • Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and meet strict deadlines in a dynamic business environment
    • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English to effectively collaborate with internal and external partners
    • Proficient working knowledge of Microsoft Office products with advanced Microsoft Excel functions

Nice to Have

    • HRIS & Payroll Systems: Hands-on experience with major global HRIS and ERP systems (e.g., Workday or NetSuite)

jobs.title: Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) Manager
jobs.excerpt: Releaf (www. releaf. co. uk) is an innovative, regulated online medical cannabis clinic serving 20,000+ patients.
jobs.description:
Releaf (www.releaf.co.uk) is an innovative, regulated online medical cannabis clinic serving 20,000+

patients. We specialise in the fast, efficient delivery of high-quality medication and exceptional patient

care. We are a company of around 170 people, and we are building the finance function that will take

the business to its next stage of scale.

We are an AI-first finance team. We have rolled out Claude across the finance function, and it is already

part of how we produce Board packs, investor updates, analysis and reviews. We are looking for

someone who will take that further, not someone we need to convince.

Role overview

We are hiring an FP&A Manager to own financial planning, forecasting and performance reporting

across the group. This is the first dedicated FP&A role at Releaf. A target plan and commercial models

are already in place. You will take ownership of their preparation, develop them into a full driver-based

planning model, and set the standard for how planning and reporting work as we scale.

You will report to the Finance & Commercial Director and work directly with the CFO and the Board,

with no direct reports initially. Within your first year you will own the preparation of the budget, the

rolling forecast, the monthly performance and Board packs, and the group cash flow model. The Group

Finance Manager owns month-end close, accounting policy, accruals and the statutory audit; you will

provide forecast and commercial inputs to the close, and work closely with them on reconciled

numbers.

This role suits someone with at least three years post-qualification experience who has done FP&A inside a

larger business, or a business that has scaled, and now wants the whole discipline rather than a slice of

it. You already use AI tools in your day-to-day work, you have opinions on where they help and where

they do not, and you are energised rather than alarmed by a business with ambitions to grow

substantially from its current level.

How the finance team uses AI today

Claude is in daily use across the finance team. Current uses include:

  • Board packs: drafting and reviewing commentary, checking the numbers tie through, and

challenging the narrative before it goes to the Board

  • Investor updates: building investor materials and update packs from the underlying model
  • Analysis and modelling: variance analysis, cohort and unit economics work, scenario

modelling and model review

  • Contracts and commercial: first-pass review of supplier, manufacturing and commercial

agreements, with the risks flagged for a human decision

  • Operational finance: reconciliations, month-on-month file comparisons, working papers and

data clean-up

The FP&A Manager will be expected to use these tools from the first week, and to make them a

standard, documented part of how planning and reporting get done.

Key responsibilities

1. Planning, budgeting and forecasting

  • Own the development process and preparation of the annual budget and the quarterly re-forecast,

built on business drivers

  • Own the preparation and reporting of the rolling three-month revenue and gross margin forecast,

and be accountable for its accuracy

  • Own the preparation of the group cashflow forecast, including working capital, stock purchasing and

intercompany flows across the Group

  • Support the Finance & Commercial Director on target-setting, and report performance against both

budget and target

  • Build scenario and sensitivity analysis into the planning process so the Board sees a range, not a

single line

2. Performance reporting and the Board pack

  • Own the production of the monthly performance reporting pack end to end — revenue, gross

margin, cost of sales, overheads, cash and the operational KPIs that drive them

  • Prepare the monthly Board pack and slide deck, including commentary, for review and sign-off by

the Finance & Commercial Director. Use AI to speed up drafting and review, while remaining

accountable for the accuracy of every number

  • Own the monthly cost of sales analysis and the margin bridge — price, volume, mix, discount,

freight and fulfilment

  • Report on the commercial performance of the international entities as they become material
  • Issue a mid-month flash on revenue, gross margin and cash ahead of the full pack
  • Support investor updates with consistent, reconciled numbers and clear narrative

3. Finance data, systems and AI

  • Own the design, development and maintenance of a single, governed finance data warehouse,

bringing together Xero, Spendesk, Stripe and Releafs ERP, so the finance team can use reliable

data in reporting, analysis and AI models. This includes data quality, reconciliation to the ledger,

access controls and the exclusion or anonymisation of patient-identifiable data

  • Own the implementation and management of AI initiatives across the finance team. Set the

roadmap with the Finance & Commercial Director and CFO, build AI into planning and reporting,

and deliver reusable workflows, including prompts for variance commentary, the flash, pack review,

reconciliations and data preparation. Train the team and measure the time released and accuracy

gained

  • Lead the automation of reporting across Xero, Spendesk, Stripe and Releafs own ERP, replacing

manual consolidation with something that runs

  • Working with the Group Finance Manager, identify where AI can remove manual effort from the

close and reporting cycle, deliver it, and measure the time it releases

  • Set and apply sensible guardrails for AI use in finance — human review of outputs, a clear audit

trail, and the right handling of commercially sensitive and patient-related data in a regulated

healthcare business

  • Map and upgrade the end-to-end planning and reporting workflow; document controls,

assumptions, AI workflows and change logs

4. Commercial partnering

  • Own unit economics and cohort analysis (CAC, LTV, retention) to support commercial and

marketing decisions

  • Translate the numbers for non-finance leaders, and be willing to challenge them
  • Support the Finance & Commercial Director on departmental cost analysis and budgeting for

Marketing, Clinic, Operations and IT

  • Contribute to business cases and investment appraisal
  • Help colleagues outside finance get more from AI for their own reporting and analysis

What success looks like in year one

  • A trusted planning model. A driver-based budget and rolling three-month revenue and gross

margin forecast that the Board uses to make decisions, with forecast accuracy measured and

reported every month.

  • A Board and management pack that runs like clockwork. The monthly performance and Board

packs land on a fixed date.

  • Full cash visibility. A group cashflow forecast that gives the Board a reliable view of cash and

working capital across the Company.

  • A finance data and AI foundation. A governed data warehouse in live use, manual consolidation

removed, and documented AI workflows with the hours they release measured.

Requirements

Essential

  • Fully qualified ACA, ACCA or CIMA with at least three years post-qualification experience
  • Demonstrable ownership of budgeting, forecasting and management or Board reporting — not
    •

support of someone else's

  • Demonstrable production of Board packs and presentation of financial performance to senior

leadership, with clear, decision-focused commentary

  • Advanced Excel: driver-based modelling, including with large datasets. You should be able to build

a three-statement or driver model from scratch

  • Hands-on, current experience of using AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot in

your own finance work — for example drafting Board or management commentary, building and

checking models, analysing large datasets, reviewing documents or automating reporting. You will

be asked to walk us through real examples at interview

  • Sound judgement on AI output: you know where it is reliable, where it is not, and you check before

you rely on it

Welcome to MICE DESK

﻿

MICE DESK is the leading European company automating the sales process in the hospitality industry — and we are now expanding to the US.

Our platform, Rocket, turns event, meeting, and group inquiries into autonomous end-to- end workflows: from RFP to signed contract, across email, CRM, and PMS systems. We integrate with the systems hotels actually run on — Oracle OPERA Cloud, SIHOT, Guestline, Salesforce, Marriott's enterprise stack — which means our engineers work inside real hotel operations, not against sandbox APIs.

We are a Series A-stage company with a deliberately small team and real enterprise traction: major hotel groups across Europe run their group sales on Rocket. The people joining now shape the product, the deployment playbook, and the culture.

﻿

﻿The Role

QA Automation Engineers are how Rocket stays reliable at scale. You build the automation frameworks, testing infrastructure, and quality processes that allow Engineering to ship quickly without compromising stability.

This is an automation-first role focused on building quality into every stage of the development lifecycle. You work closely with Engineering, Product, and DevOps to ensure every feature, integration, and release is validated through automated testing before it reaches production.

If you enjoy designing automation systems, solving complex engineering problems, and creating the foundations that enable fast, confident software delivery, this is the role.

What You Will Own
﻿

1. Test automation, end-to-end.

Own the strategy and implementation of automated testing across the platform. Design scalable automation frameworks for UI, API, integration, and end-to-end testing, continuously increasing automated test coverage while ensuring tests remain reliable, maintainable, and efficient.

2. CI/CD quality engineering.

Build quality directly into the deployment pipeline by integrating automated testing throughout the CI/CD process. Establish quality gates, monitor test execution, improve developer feedback loops, and reduce release risk through continuous validation.

3. Platform quality and reliability.

Ensure the reliability of Rocket's distributed systems by validating APIs, integrations, backend services, and AI-powered workflows. Develop regression, smoke, and integration testing strategies while identifying quality risks early in the development lifecycle.

4. Engineering collaboration.

Partner closely with Engineering and Product throughout feature development. Promote testability, establish automation best practices, participate in technical design discussions, and help build a culture where quality is a shared engineering responsibility.

5. Continuous improvement.

Continuously evolve our quality engineering practices by introducing modern automation tools, improving testing processes, strengthening regression coverage, and driving automation-first thinking across the engineering organization.

Who You Are
﻿

Must-have

  • 5+ years of experience in Quality Engineering or QA Automation
  • Strong experience designing and building automation frameworks from scratch
  • Hands-on experience with API, integration, UI, and end-to-end test automation
  • Strong programming or scripting skills (JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Java, or similar)
  • Experience with modern automation tools such as Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, or equivalent
  • Experience integrating automated testing into CI/CD pipelines
  • Strong understanding of software testing methodologies and quality engineering principles
  • Experience testing distributed systems, REST APIs, and asynchronous workflows
  • Strong analytical and debugging skills
  • Excellent English communication skills (B2–C1)
    ﻿

Nice-to-have

  • Experience testing AI-powered or LLM-based applications
  • Experience with performance or load testing tools
  • Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, and cloud environments
  • Familiarity with contract testing and API mocking
  • Experience working in high-growth product startups
  • Knowledge of hospitality technology or enterprise SaaS platforms

Hiring Process

  1. Intro interview — background, engineering experience, automation expertise, and motivation for joining MICE DESK
  2. Technical interview — automation frameworks, testing strategies, CI/CD integration, quality engineering practices, and real-world automation challenges
  3. Founder interview — engineering culture, ownership, product quality, and your role in building a reliable AI-native platform

Why MICE DESK

  • Own quality engineering for one of Europe's leading AI platforms for hospitality sales automation—now expanding into the US
  • Build the automation frameworks and quality systems that enable rapid, reliable software delivery
  • Work closely with Engineering, Product, and DevOps on modern technologies and AI-powered workflows

We are in the middle of a significant transformation. FIS is investing heavily in building proprietary fraud signals, next-generation machine learning models, and AI-driven detection capabilities — not simply integrating third-party tools, but constructing a differentiated, data-rich fraud intelligence platform from the ground up. This role is central to that work, and the person who fills it will have an outsized impact on how FIS competes and serves its clients for years to come.

The Role

The VP, Product will own the product roadmap and strategy for FIS’s Enterprise Fraud & Financial Crimes portfolio. The position will report to the SVP of Fraud & Financial Crimes and lead a team of product managers, each leading their own PM teams across the portfolio.

This is a role for someone who has built and run product at a fraud or financial crimes company — someone who knows what a modern, technically differentiated fraud roadmap looks like, has shipped it, and is ready to bring that standard to one of the largest financial technology platforms in the world.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the end-to-end product roadmap for the Enterprise Fraud & Financial Crimes portfolio
  • Set product strategy that reflects the full breadth of the portfolio. Your depth in transaction monitoring will raise the bar across the platform, but this role is not transaction monitoring alone, it spans the entire fraud and financial crimes stack.
  • Partner directly with FIS’s Data & AI product leads to define and drive the roadmap for proprietary fraud models, signals, and intelligence capabilities — a central pillar of FIS’s platform transformation.
  • Lead a senior product management organization spanning multiple product lines, providing clear ownership, strategic direction, and career development across the team.
  • Drive enterprise architecture and product strategy to ensure the platform scales to support financial institutions of every size, configurable to diverse client needs while maintaining a coherent long-term vision.
  • Engage directly with clients — from the largest global banks to community institutions — to validate priorities, understand needs, and surface outside-in perspective into the roadmap.
  • Align cross-functional teams across engineering, data science, compliance, operations, and commercial to deliver coordinated product outcomes.
  • Connect product decisions to business results — client adoption, revenue growth, fraud detection effectiveness, false-positive reduction, and measurable client outcomes.

What We’re Looking For

  • A product leader who has built fraud products. You have owned a roadmap at a fraud technology company, a fintech, or a financial institution where product was the core discipline. You know what modern fraud product looks like because you have shipped it. A background leading fraud product strategy at a cutting-edge fraud or financial crimes company is highly valued, as is experience leading fraud product at a financial institution or payments company — provided you owned the roadmap, not solely operations.
  • Deep transaction monitoring expertise. You understand the mechanics of rules engines, behavioral signals, and ML-based detection across cards and money movement. This is your strongest domain, and it shows — but you think in terms of the full portfolio, not just one capability.
  • Experience building proprietary fraud models and signals. You have led the product side of building proprietary fraud detection models and signals: defining which data and signals matter, partnering with data science to develop and productionize models, and turning them into differentiated capabilities clients rely on. You treat models and signals as products, with their own roadmaps, performance metrics, and feedback loops.
  • Breadth across the fraud and financial crimes stack. You understand end-customer authentication, identity, AML and financial crimes, and how these capabilities fit together into a coherent, enterprise-grade platform.
  • Technical fluency. You do not need to write code, but you need to be the kind of product leader who gets into architecture conversations, challenges technical tradeoffs, and drives roadmaps alongside engineering and data science. You have managed technical teams and held them accountable to delivery.
  • Commercial and enterprise orientation. You understand how to build products that serve large, complex enterprise clients and how product decisions translate to revenue, adoption, and client value.
  • Executive presence and stakeholder credibility. You can operate at the client C-suite level and internally across a large, matrixed organization.

Nice to Have

  • Experience as a head of product or equivalent at a fraud technology company or fraud-focused fintech.
  • Background leading fraud product at a financial institution or large payments company, with direct ownership of the product roadmap.
  • Familiarity with integrated fraud and AML transaction monitoring platforms.
  • Experience building or scaling AI, ML, or rules-based fraud detection products.

Core Responsibilities – Growth (50%)

Strategic Partnerships Strategy & Growth Planning

  • Support the development of the value proposition and partnership thesis for target partners — articulating the clinical, financial, and operational case for partnership for executive audiences.
  • Build and maintain a forward-looking view of the partnership landscape, including competitive JV activity, at-risk incumbent relationships, and white-space systems where no outpatient partner is entrenched.

De Novo Growth: Top-of-Funnel Orchestration

  • Orchestrate the top of the funnel for the de novo development pipeline — establishing the process, cadence, and criteria by which new-site opportunities are surfaced, screened, and advanced into formal approval.
  • Coordinate with regional and market leaders to drive geographic prioritization, reconciling local market knowledge with an enterprise-level framework for where de novo investment creates the most durable competitive advantage.
  • Own the front-end market evaluation methodology: define and continuously refine the analytical inputs (demographics, procedure demand and modality mix, payer landscape, competitive density, referral base, CON environment, real estate and access considerations) that determine market attractiveness and site viability.
  • Work with corporate development to build the commercial case for prioritized de novo opportunities — synthesizing market analysis, demand modeling, and volume ramp assumptions into a clear, defensible investment thesis.
  • Standardize how opportunities are packaged for review, creating a consistent set of criteria and deliverables so that leadership evaluates de novo candidates across regions.
  • Maintain the enterprise de novo opportunity pipeline as a managed portfolio — providing visibility into stage, priority, and expected value, and ensuring a healthy, continuously replenished funnel.

Commercial Excellence (50%)

Sales Training & Onboarding

Job Description

A bit about this role:


  • The Senior Manager of Payment Integrity is responsible for data-driven research and root-cause analyses related to payment integrity provider disputes and escalations to facilitate resolution and drive education in support of Devoted’s collaborative provider relationships.
  • In this role, the Senior Manager directly oversees Payment Integrity disputes and appeals delivery teams. This role will own day-to-day operations and support, including end-to-end queue management, operational timeliness, quality assurance, training, and strict adherence to service level agreements (SLAs).
  • The Senior Manager partners closely with leadership and operational support teams to ensure edits, audits, and reviews are executed properly while monitoring compliance with organizational and regulatory standards.

Your Responsibilities and Impact will include:

  • Operational & SLA Management: Direct, mentor, and oversee the Payment Integrity (PI) disputes and appeals delivery team, driving daily queue health, turnaround times, quality assurance, and strict SLA compliance across all claim disputes and escalations.
  • Dual-Track Subject Matter Expertise: Serve as the definitive Subject Matter Expert (SME) on complex billing guidelines, reimbursement policies, and CMS regulations (e.g., NCCI, LCD/NCDs), acting as the primary point of escalation for delivery teams and internal cross-functional partners on high-complexity claims.
  • Root-Cause & Trend Analysis: Perform granular trend analyses on dispute data—evaluating CPT/HCPCS codes, modifiers, billing taxonomy, facilities, and regions—to identify volume spikes, billing errors, and underlying system or policy root causes.
  • Upstream Synergy & Policy Optimization: Translate dispute and appeal insights into actionable recommendations for upstream PI edit and audit teams to refine logic, eliminate policy ambiguities, reduce overturn rates, and mitigate future dispute volume over time.
  • Leadership Reporting & Escalations: Represent Payment Integrity dispute performance to senior leadership through clear operational reporting and trend updates; step in directly to resolve high-priority provider escalations.
  • Audit Readiness & Governance: Maintain rigorous documentation logs, SOPs, and quality control frameworks for claim research to ensure continuous audit readiness for CMS program audits, state regulatory reviews, and internal compliance evaluations.
  • External Provider Enablement: Collaborate across clinical, coding, and operational teams to leverage payment integrity dispute findings into targeted external billing guidance, clear policy documentation, and provider education.
  • Process Modernization: Identify opportunities to leverage AI tools, automation, and LLM-assisted workflows to accelerate research, improve log quality, and streamline daily operational throughput.

Required skills and experience:

  • 5+ Years of Healthcare PI & Dispute Experience: Proven track record in healthcare payment integrity, provider dispute management, coding/clinical documentation review, or claim audit operations.
  • 3+ Years of supervisory or people management experience.
  • Deep CMS & Coding Expertise: Extensive mastery of CMS regulations governing Medicare Advantage disputes, organization determinations, and auditing protocols, paired with expert-level knowledge of CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10, UB-04, NCCI edits, and NCD/LCD guidelines.
  • Balanced SME & Operational Leadership: Demonstrated ability to manage operational metrics, queue throughput, and team performance while simultaneously serving as the high-level SME for complex medical record reviews and coding/clinical determinations.
  • Root-Cause Analytics & Data Proficiency: Strong analytical background in synthesizing claims data, research findings, and medical records to identify systematic gaps, establish defensible audit decisions, and drive upstream process fixes.
  • Enterprise Collaboration & Communication: Exceptional cross-functional collaboration skills with a track record of aligning processes across enterprise dispute, clinical, audit, and leadership teams, as well as presenting complex performance metrics to executives.

Desired skills and experience:

  • Active medical coding certification from AAPC or AHIMA (e.g., CPC, CIC, COC, or RHIA/RHIT)
  • Hands-on experience or familiarity with implementing LLMs, AI-driven claim intake tools, or process automation (RPA) to optimize log tracking, research efficiency, and operational speed.
  • Familiarity with healthcare data tools (e.g., SQL, Tableau, Power BI) or claim editing engine logic (e.g., Cotiviti, Optum, Change Healthcare)
  • Prior experience in Provider Relations or Network Management, with a knack for turning technical payment integrity findings into clear, digestible provider-facing education materials and billing guidance.
  • Proven conflict resolution skills when negotiating complex, high-dollar, or executive-level provider escalations.
  • AI & Automation Aptitude: Practical experience or strong curiosity and hands-on aptitude for adopting AI tools, automation, and LLM-based workflows to increase team productivity, efficiency, and operational accuracy.

Location: Remote (United States). Approximately 10% to 15% travel for practice visits, seller meetings and closings

Position Summary

Associated Veterinary Partners is in growth mode. We are a founder-led, well-funded acquirer of veterinary hospitals with close to ten practices under LOI today and a deep pipeline behind them. We were built by a former Carlyle Group investment professional and an entrepreneurial veterinarian, and our model is highly differentiated: we partner with doctors (co-ownership), preserve clinical autonomy, and structure every deal for the long term.

Today, the founders lead M&A department with support from the Partnership Manager and Partnership Analyst. We are hiring one person to own the function end to end: pipeline management, initial diligence and underwriting, LOI, confirmatory diligence, and closing. You will be the most senior person on M&A after the founders. This is a builder's seat with real ownership and a pipeline waiting for you.

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the pipeline of record and the weekly M&A cadence. Instill a sense of urgency and ensure transactions are moving forward.
  • Work closely with and mentor Partnership Manager and Partnership Analyst.
  • Review deal workbooks for every opportunity, apply AVP's transaction review framework, and put a clear recommendation on price, structure and risk in front of the CEO and COO.
  • Draft IOIs and LOIs and negotiate business terms with sellers and their advisors, including seller notes, partner-doctor buy-ins, earnouts, and other (e.g. real estate leases).
  • Run diligence across financial, tax, legal, HR, licensing, real estate and systems, and manage outside counsel, accountants and other stakeholders to a timeline and a budget.
  • Support the CEO on definitive agreements (issues list, business points, disclosure schedules) and own the closing: checklist, funds flow, entity setup, lender deliverables and board consents.
  • Partner with the COO on partner-doctor employment agreements and buy-ins. Run the post-closing reconciliation and hand a clean file to operations and finance.
  • Own the M&A section of board materials and support the CEO on investor, lender and capital planning work.
  • Build the playbooks and use AI tools proactively so deals move faster with a lean team.

Core competencies

  • Valuation and Deal Modeling. Builds and defends the practice acquisition model: normalized EBITDA, DVM production, working capital, lease terms.
  • Deal Structuring and Negotiation. Recommends price and structure (seller notes, buy-ins, earnouts, put and call mechanics, ), drafts IOIs and LOIs, and negotiates business terms with sellers and their advisors.
  • Diligence Leadership and Risk Judgment. Runs diligence across financial, tax, legal, HR, licensing, real estate and systems. Proactively tackles problems and tries to find solutions before escalating to CEO or COO. Think critically, and come up with decision trees based on the nature of the issue at hand:: walk away, reprice, restructure or fix post-close.
  • Transaction Execution and Process Discipline. Runs LOI to close as a project: third parties, timeline, budget, funds flow, closing deliverables, post-closing reconciliation. Uses AI tools to compress cycle time and builds playbooks so deals move without the CEO.
  • Legal and Documentation Fluency. Reads purchase agreements, leases, employment agreements and seller notes closely enough to catch inconsistencies with the LOI and the model. Owns the issues list and disclosure schedules.
  • Seller and Practice-Owner Relationship Management. Earns the trust of veterinarians who have spent decades building their practice. Plain talk, patience, fast honest answers, follow-through. Converts relationships into signed LOIs and keeps sellers engaged through close.
  • Pipeline and Team Leadership. Directs the Partnerships Manager and Analyst, owns the pipeline of record and the weekly M&A meeting, sets expectations, reviews the work and raises the bar.
  • Executive Communication and Board Materials. Writes deal memos, board consents and the M&A section of board materials that a sophisticated investor can read in five minutes and approve. Brings a recommendation and the reasoning.

Experience

  • 6 to 10 years of transaction experience across investment banking, private equity and corporate development, including at least two years in investment banking or private equity deal execution. Corporate development at a multi-site consolidator is strongly preferred.
  • A record of closing lower middle market deals end to end. Healthcare services or veterinary experience preferred; other owner-operated, multi-site roll-ups are relevant.
  • Self-directed and accountable. Practice owners see patients during the day, so seller calls run in the evening and closings run to the wire. In this role, hours and intensity will fluctuate. This is a deal role with deal hours, built for someone who wants ownership.
  • Bachelor's degree required. MBA, CFA or CPA useful but not required.

How this role works with the founders

You own full cycle of execution: lead to LOI and LOI to close, including diligence and everything that comes with it. The CEO keeps final approval on price and structure and leads negotiation of definitive agreements with counsel. The COO owns partner-doctor relationships.

    • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision & Life Insurance Options
    • Unlimited/Flexible PTO
    • 401(k) + up to 6% company match

Position Title: Evaluation Technical Advisor

Department: Program and Innovation Office

FLSA Classification: Exempt

Reports to: Senior Technical Advisor

Position Highlights

Location: Remote, must be based in the United States. Up to 20% of domestic travel may be required.

Salary Range: $80,000-$95,000, plus benefits

Position Type: Grant funded, limited-term opportunity contingent upon funding

Position Start Date: Immediate availability desired

Position End Date: July 31, 2027

Overview

The CDC Foundation seeks a full-time Evaluation Technical Advisor to support an evaluation capacity-building project for non-governmental Veteran-serving organizations (VSOs) that are implementing programs aligned with a public health approach to suicide prevention. This position will work closely with Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) subject matter experts and CDC Foundation project staff to provide expert-level support and guidance, acting as a key resource to funded project grantees in developing their capacity to plan and conduct evaluations of their veteran suicide prevention programs.

The Technical Advisor will leverage expertise and experience in program evaluation to assess the evaluation capacity building needs of the funded organizations and work with partners to develop and implement engaging, culturally appropriate and impactful capacity building in response to those needs. The ideal candidate will be able to provide technical oversight on all types of evaluations and performance monitoring deliverables. Strong communication and teamwork skills are of absolute importance to succeed in this role. The Technical Advisor will also help the project and CDC Foundation Evaluation Team design and develop internal evaluation plans, design effective and impactful internal evaluations and facilitate translation of data to action in practice for continuous improvement and refinement.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provide subject matter expertise on evaluation concepts and methods and maintains a working knowledge of established evaluation frameworks and guidelines.
  • Co-lead and design approach to capacity building and technical assistance to program grantees
  • Advise, partner with and coach grantees to strengthen competencies for strong, ongoing program evaluation, in collaboration with CDC and the CDC Foundation program staff
  • Provide consistent, tailored and direct technical assistance to grantees on the development and implementation of evaluation plans for prioritized program areas, including the development of evaluation questions and frameworks and appropriate evaluation data collection instrument tools for program evaluations
  • Supervise and support collection and analysis of data for program evaluation in accordance with timeframes set forth in program and evaluation work plans
  • Review and provide written feedback on evaluation deliverables
  • Oversee the design and implementation of performance and impact evaluations for the capacity building project
  • Represent the CDC Foundation and the project team at partnership events
  • Participate in and/or lead special projects and other duties as assigned
  • Travel for in-person training and program meetings to support capacity building activities such as site-visits, partner convenings, conferences and other dissemination efforts, etc.

Qualifications and Necessary Skills

  • Master's degree in public health, public administration, community development, program measurement & evaluation, public policy or other related field
  • Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in monitoring and evaluation with a focus on integrating evidence building into upstream public health programs
  • Experience in suicide prevention and/or working with military and veteran communities is strongly preferred
  • Experience with developing logic models, identifying indicators, designing and implementing data collection instruments and processes and creating evaluation reports
  • Demonstrate the ability to conduct evaluation from start to finish including stakeholder engagement, program definition, evaluation design, evidence gathering and conclusion
  • Proficiency with both quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis methodologies and monitoring best practices
  • Knowledge of or familiarity with the CDC Framework for Program Evaluation in Public Health and the American Evaluation Association’s Guiding Principles for Evaluators
  • Experience managing or overseeing capacity building efforts, technical assistance or advice and guidance through appropriate training and engagement with grantees
  • Ability to engage with, listen to and learn from a broad range of evaluation stakeholders, encouraging their meaningful participation
  • Ability to communicate in a clear, positive manner with external partners, as well as clearly communicating evaluation strategies and implications to non-technical audiences
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to listen well and effectively represent the organization and its mission
  • Creativity, problem solving, demonstrated ability to effectively collaborate with others
  • Ability to take initiative and be a creative problem-solver.
  • Demonstrated ability to work well independently and within teams.
  • Demonstrated experience working with remote partners and teams.
  • Excellent organization and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously with competing timelines.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, mental or physical disabilities, veteran status, and all other characteristics protected by law. We comply with all applicable laws including E.O. 11246 and the Vietnam[EA1] Era Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974 governing employment practices and do not discriminate on the basis of any unlawful criteria in accordance with 41 C.F.R. §§ 60-300.5(a)(12) and 60-741.5(a)(7). As a federal government contractor, we take affirmative action on behalf of protected veterans.

The CDC Foundation is a smoke-free environment.

Relocation expenses are not included.

About the CDC Foundation

The CDC Foundation is an independent nonprofit authorized by Congress to mobilize philanthropic partners to support the public health system, including the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in preventing and responding to threats to health. In this role, we are focused on one priority: building catalytic, flexible and impactful partnerships—with corporations, philanthropies, individuals and organizations—to help improve the health and lives of people in all communities, everywhere. Full-time Assistant or Associate Professor, or Professor of Practice in Educational Counseling & Academic Program Director (APD) – Remote, USA

The Department of ABA, School Psychology, and Educational Counseling (ASPEC), in the Sanford College of Education (SCOE) at National University invites applications for an Assistant or an Associate in Educational Counseling. Rank is commensurate with qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will have a potential or demonstrated record of excellence in teaching and scholarship in their field and a commitment to serving the university’s diverse adult student body. This position is remote with no residency requirements. This position works closely with other faculty within the discipline and administration contributing to programmatic strategies that ensure program quality, student engagement, and success.

The Academic Program Director (APD) is a full-time faculty member who directs the strategy, operations and support for the degree program for which this role is responsible. As the primary spokesperson for all program (part-time and full-time) faculty and students, the APD will act as the primary source of information about specific programmatic strategies, needs and daily operations and initiate and approve changes to ensure program quality, driving student engagement and success. The APD serves as the lead discipline expert for the program as well as primary contact for multiple stakeholders. This position collaborates with program faculty in support of student success, as well as the Director of Assessment to conduct program assessment on a regular basis to ensure the program is meeting the needs of the student and the program’s related industries and where applicable, the programmatic accreditation requirements. This position ensures the incorporation of identified trends or changes into the curriculum, in collaboration with the Director of Curriculum, and serves in either a direct or consulting role during course development, updating, and maintenance. The APD meets regularly with the College leadership (Department Chair/Associate Dean and/or Dean) to ensure that the program aligns with University and College goals and priorities.

In lieu of scholarship requirements, if you are selected as the candidate, you may be considered for a Professor of Practice position.

Essential Functions:

Candidates will be evaluated for their level of proficiency and potential (for excellence) in teaching, scholarship, and service. The main expectations of this position include:

Teaching

  • Teach and develop online or onsite courses in the following areas: Counseling theories, counseling law and ethics, current issues in school and college counseling, program review, crisis intervention, trauma in youth, social and cultural issues, career development, group counseling and assessment and evaluation.
  • Maintain pedagogical and subject matter expertise in the instructor’s field.
  • Create an inclusive and positive learning environment for diverse learners.
  • Ensure course and program practices align with compliance and accreditation standards.
  • Adhere to the National University’s academic integrity policy.

Scholarship

  • Maintain a productive scholarship agenda suitable to a teaching university.
  • Engage in scholarly activities to maintain professional growth.
  • Participate in professional development as outlined in faculty policies.

Service

  • Participate in curriculum oversight, shared governance, and the student experience.
  • Serve on committees at the program, department, college or/and university level and engage in community activities that promote program outreach and university goals.
  • Participate in program meetings and advisory boards to integrate best practices and strategic initiatives.
  • Responsible for annual program reviews and attending departmental and college level meetings as a representative of the program.

The ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications:

Education & Experience:

Required Qualifications:

  • Terminal degree e.g. Ph.D or Ed.D. degree in Educational Counseling or related discipline, required.
  • Leadership experience as a director or coordinator of a school counseling graduate program.
  • Understanding of school counselor roles in California public schools.
  • Experience with online education.
  • Current California PPS credential in school counseling.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Specialization in Community College Counseling is preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience navigating and interpreting California Commission on Teacher. Credentialing (CCTC) policies for Pupil Personnel Services (PPS) credentialing.

Special conditions of employment include:

  • Background check required.
  • Travel is required at least once annually to attend the annual Commencement ceremony (if held onsite).

For full consideration, interested candidates should provide the following:

  • A cover letter that includes experience as a program leader in school counseling
  • A curriculum vita
  • Statement of teaching experience online and/or onsite for a diverse student body.

Candidate receiving offers will be offered a salary/pay rate commensurate with experience that vary based on a candidate’s qualifications, skills, and competencies. Absent exceptional circumstances, candidates will be offered a salary within this range for this position. Base pay is one component of National University’s total rewards package, as we are dedicated to supporting the needs of the “whole you” with our holistic approach to employee benefits by offering comprehensive well-being benefits for you and your family. For full details about our benefit plan offerings, please visit . For part-time positions, please click here.

National University is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant per applicable federal, state and local laws. At NU, a mix of highly talented, innovative, and creative people come together to make the impact of a lifetime for each of our student learners. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment, education, and admission at National University.

jobs.description:
Fabula is a fast-growing D2C coffee brand in the United States. We're looking for a Head of Growth aka killer performance media buyer/creative strategist who is already operating at a high level in eCommerce. This isn't a role for someone who wants to learn how to scale an eCommerce brand. We want someone who has already done it.

Our goal is simple: bring in someone who can jump in, take ownership of our growth engine, and take Fabula to the next level.

What you'll own

  • Paid media: Own and scale Meta as the primary acquisition channel, with additional experience across Google and/or TikTok Paid
  • Creative strategy: Identify winning customer angles, hooks, messaging, formats, and concepts based on performance data and customer research
  • Creative testing: Build and manage a systematic testing pipeline and rapidly identify winning creatives
  • Full-funnel performance: Analyze and optimize the entire journey from ad advertorial/landing page offer conversion
  • Research: Mine customer reviews, surveys, Reddit, competitor ads, Meta Ads Library, and other sources for new angles and opportunities
  • Creative production: Brief and manage UGC creators, editors, and designers - while remaining hands-on with scripts, hooks, copy, and creative direction
  • Performance analysis: Make daily decisions around what to scale, iterate, or kill based on CPA, ROAS, CTR, hook rate, thumbstop rate, CVR, contribution margin, and other relevant metrics
  • Scaling: Take proven creative and media-buying strategies and turn them into significant increases in profitable spend
  • Funnels: Work on advertorials, landing pages, VSLs, offers, and other conversion assets to improve overall acquisition efficiency
  • AI: Use AI aggressively to accelerate research, creative ideation, scripting, production, analysis, and workflows

What success looks like

We don't measure activity; we measure results. This is a 100% performance role focused on scaling spend while maintaining CAC ceiling.

Success means:

  • Scaling paid spend while maintaining healthy unit economics
  • Improving ROAS and reducing CPA
  • Increasing creative win rate and testing velocity
  • Finding new winning angles and audiences
  • Improving conversion rates across the funnel
  • Building a repeatable creative and media-buying system
  • Ultimately, taking Fabula to the next level

You are

  • 4–6+ years of experience creating performance creatives for D2C/eCommerce brands or eCommerce agencies (not B2B, not a generalist)
  • A proven Meta media buyer who has personally scaled campaigns, not just overseen them (at least $50k/month in ad spend)
  • Equally strong on creative strategy and performance marketing
  • Deeply experienced with direct-response advertising and customer psychology
  • Able to look at an ad account, creative performance, and funnel data and immediately identify what needs to change
  • Experienced scaling DTC/eCommerce brands - not B2B, SaaS, lead generation, or general marketing
  • Hands-on with creative: you can write or heavily edit hooks, scripts, headlines, briefs, and landing page copy
  • Experienced managing creative production with UGC creators, editors, and designers
  • An operator, not a consultant. You don't just make recommendations - you execute, test, learn, and scale
  • Comfortable working directly with founders and taking significant ownership with minimal hand-holding
  • AI-native: you use AI daily to accelerate research, creative development, analysis, and execution
  • Fast-moving, highly analytical, and obsessed with finding what works

Strong bonus points

  • Experience scaling supplements, health, wellness, beauty, or other DTC consumer brands
  • Experience with advertorials, VSLs, or aggressive direct-response funnels
  • Experience with TikTok Paid / Spark Ads
  • Experience with Outbrain or Taboola
  • Experience with tools such as Triple Whale, Northbeam, Motion, Foreplay, or similar
  • Strong understanding of FTC/FDA considerations for supplement advertising

Important: Who this role is NOT for

This is not a fit if:

  • You've managed less than $200K/month in ad spend
  • Your background is primarily organic social or influencer marketing
  • You're primarily a creative strategist who doesn't understand media buying
  • You're primarily a media buyer who relies on someone else for all creative strategy
  • You've worked mainly in B2B, SaaS, lead generation, or non-eCommerce environments
  • You're looking for a role where someone else tells you what to do

We want someone who can walk into an eCommerce brand, look at the numbers and the creative, figure out what's broken, and start making it better immediately.

Schedule

  • Fully remote
  • Full-time
  • Minimum 6-hour overlap with US Eastern Time (10:00 AM–4:00 PM ET)
  • Direct collaboration with the founders
  • Significant ownership and autonomy
  • Possible equity upside for strong performance

Work at Home Bilingual Vietnamese-English Video-Phone Interpreter

Location: Work at Home position in United States

Position Overview:

The Vietnamese Video-Telephone- Interpreter is responsible for handling calls on demand, and renders the meaning of conversations between Vietnamese and English speakers. The interpreter breaks the communication barrier in a wide range of industries that LanguageLine Solutions serves: Healthcare, Government, Insurance, Financial, Utilities, Travel & Hospitality, General Business, Law Enforcement, Court, and 911.

The interpreter processes information quickly, concisely and recognizes sensitive cultural differences. The interpreter is professional and courteous at all times and uses appropriate terminology and understands common industry procedures and practices. The video and audio interpreting sessions may involve simple or complex, technical or non-technical subjects.

This position does not involve written translation however translators and other skilled linguists are encouraged to apply. The interpreters translate verbally.

**This is a remote position. The Interpreter works from his/her home-office. It is essential to ensure a quiet & secure environment**

Essential Job Functions:

  • Respond to video and audio interpreting sessions promptly and conduct interpretation in a friendly and professional manner.

  • Speak clearly in both languages using proper pronunciation, enunciation and polite expressions.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor throughout the video and audio interpreting sessions at all times.
  • Remain calm during video and audio interpreting sessions in the event that one of the primary speakers is incoherent or upset, especially in emergency situations such as 911 calls.
  • Maintain punctuality and availability during scheduled work hours.
  • Follow client instructions, in compliance with protocol to ensure client expectations are met with the Limited English-speaking Person (LEP), avoiding interaction with the LEP without client’s permission.
  • Understand protocol and terminology for various industries including, but not limited to, Medical, Insurance, Finance and Law.
  • Demonstrate commitment to cultural sensitivity and working in a diverse environment.

The interpreter may need to remain on a call for extended periods without breaks due to the nature of the call or may, at times experience high call volumes.   • Excellent listening, retention and note-taking skills to maintain a high level of accuracy during interpretation.

**Based on your location, a post-offer, a pre-employment background check and/or drug screen may be required**

Medical Records

Job Industry: Charity / Social Services / Non- Profit Organization

Position Name: Medical Records Admin for Dog Rescue -( Remote Volunteer/5 hrs wk)

Job Location: Spokane, Washington, United States

Job Type: Part Time

Office Setting: Fully Remote

Remote: Yes

Compensation: Volunteer

Hours Per Week: 5 (flexible)

Role Mission

Accurate and up to date medical records are essential to providing our Rescue dogs with life saving and preventative medical care. With many volunteers working together remotely and in person, it is easy for information to get lost. This role collects data from various online platforms and enters them into a central medical record database so the whole team has access to a complete and up to date medical record.

What Winning Looks Like

Key Results Area #1 - Medical Records

  • Uploads existing electronic medical records

  • Adds medical records as appropriate for dogs who receive care

  • Protects Petstablished as the record authority

  • Sends records to veterinarians or adopters as requested

Key Results Area #2 - Communication

  • Collaborates with Intake Lead and Vaccine Scheduler for vaccines/dewormer needed at intake

  • Collaborates with Surgery Scheduler of newly admitted PHR dogs that will need S/N and/or Rabies vaccine

  • Keeps close eye on current medical cases

Needed Skills

  • Must have computer or tablet with internet access (role cannot be done with a phone)

  • Ability to learn and navigate online software and CRM

  • Comfortable with technology

  • Communicate quickly and effectively remotely

Unique Company Culture and Mission

Our Mission

At Path of Hope Rescue we save pregnant dogs and puppies from high kill shelters in the Southern United States.

Our Spokane, Washington based Rescue strives to decrease the euthanasia rate of high risk dogs in the southern United States by transporting pregnant dogs and puppies to the Pacific Northwest to find adoptive homes. We do not have a kennel or building location and are 100% foster based. We currently have two paid employees and rely heavily on volunteers and fosters as we work to build out our paid staff roles.

Our Vision.
Eliminating euthanasia of dogs in the South by decreasing the amount of dogs breeding unchecked and becoming the number one 'dog destination' in Spokane by capitalizing on Spokane's love of Rescue Dogs.

Core Values:

Transparency - sharing the good with the bad

Community - dog loving people who treat each other well

Integrity - doing what you say will do

Golden Rule - treating others how you would want to be treated

Our Company Culture

We are freedom loving American Patriots who love dogs, love freedom and love Jesus.

No NGO status here, we don't take a single penny from the government. We are 100% funded by small donors and our adoption program, with a few small private grants here and there. We built this organization from the ground up in 2018 with $87.

We are built tough and believe that hard work pays off. We're about rolling up our sleeves and taking responsibility for our own actions. We don't do drama. There are no victims here and the system isn't out to get you, the only thing standing in your way is you and your attitude. We reward merit, not DEI or pronouns. We don't bend to the cultural rot out there.

At the core of who we are, we love dogs. At PHR you will find people who recognize your dog before they recognize you. Where it's normal for your dog to have his own Instagram and people who expect to be invited to your dog's birthday party. We are focused on building a strong, positive community, one dog and one person at a time.

We know dogs are family and should be treated that way. And we are driven by a shared passion to make sure every dog who isn't being loved, finds their way to a family. We care for each other and have created a community of people who love making a difference in this world.
