Find your future with us by being a part of something bigger – leading the energy transition in building a better world for generations to come.

Imagine what you could do here. We encourage and inspire our people to embrace opportunities within our corporate office and 200 operating companies providing solutions for the utility, renewable energy, electric power, industrial, communications and government industries worldwide.

Quanta’s culture is about creating an environment where all employees can be themselves, are valued, and have an equal opportunity to succeed. When you join our team, you join a dynamic culture in which career development is encouraged, excellence is rewarded, and diversity is valued.

About this Role

JOB TITLE: Award Transition Project Manager

QUANTA COMPANY: Quanta Government Solutions, LLC

DEPARTMENT: Preconstruction Operations

LOCATION: Remote with site travel

REPORTS TO: Director, Preconstruction Operations

CLASSIFICATION: Exempt

POSITION OVERVIEW:

We are seeking an organized, hands-on project manager to run the bridge between winning a federal job and building it. From notice of award to the day construction operations takes the job, this person owns the transition schedule and every deadline in it, working with the vertical strategic lead, the Director of Construction, and our Contracts Manager. The goal is simple: every new job starts contracted and set up, with nothing left hanging from the bid.

What You'll Do

  • Run award intake within 24 hours and build one schedule of every contract deadline, including bonds, insurance, Accident Prevention Plan, Quality Control plan, baseline schedule, consent to subcontract, and submittal register.
  • Receive the sourcing file and quote package from the Procurement Manager at award, confirm it is complete (returning any gaps to Procurement the same day), and use it as the starting point for every subcontract and affiliate work order.
  • Drive every subcontract and affiliate work order to execution with the Contracts Manager, starting from the quotes gathered during the bid. Contracts drafts; you track and chase to signature.
  • Collect what each subcontractor owes before mobilizing, including prequalification, bonds, insurance, and required plans.
  • Stand up and own the commitments register through contract execution, then hand executed commitments to the Procurement Manager, who owns material and long-lead buyout through delivery.
  • Build the turnover package from the estimate and lead the handoff meeting with the vertical’s Director of Construction.
  • Coordinate job setup with Finance and PMO so the first charge lands on a fully set-up job.
  • Hold the handoff, when anything required is missing, escalate to the Director the same day, and proceed only with written waiver approval from the Director and the Director of Construction.
  • Improve the transition checklist after every job and train the people who come in behind you.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 7+ years of experience in federal construction project management, project engineering, or project startup.
  • Startup experience on USACE, NAVFAC, DOE, or comparable federal construction projects, ideally supporting Energy and Department of War work.
  • Working knowledge of federal subcontract requirements, including flowdowns, prime Miller Act bonds and subcontractor bonds, and Davis-Bacon, enough to know what complete looks like.
  • Ability to build and run a Primavera P6 schedule.
  • Strong organization and follow-through across multiple awards at once.
  • Clear written and verbal communication with project teams, subcontractors, and internal partners.
  • Procore and Costpoint experience is a plus.

jobs.excerpt: About Dean Dorton Dean Dorton’s team makes up one of the largest advisory firms in the United States.
jobs.description:
About Dean Dorton

Dean Dorton’s team makes up one of the largest advisory firms in the United States. We thrive when you thrive! We are here to help you succeed in every step of your development and career as you work with nationally recognized experts in a recognized best place to work.

Our core values guide how we work, lead, and support one another every day. They are:

  • Integrity - We do the right thing, integrity guides our decisions.
  • Relationships - We value people, relationships drive our impact.
  • Collaboration - We win as one team, collaboration fuels our success.
  • Growth - We stay curious, growth is our mindset.

About Accounting & Financial Outsourcing (AFO)

Dean Dorton's outsourced accounting team serves as a critical component to the financial success of our clients. Our team partners with organizations to serve as their CFO, controller, and/or accounting team, allowing clients to focus on other key business processes integral to their success. By offering cloud-based and real-time financial data, we translate complex financial information into meaningful advice and provide clients with the information they need to make timely strategic decisions and maintain greater control over cash flow.

Within AFO, the Equine team supports horse farms, breeding and racing operations, sales companies, and related ownership structures. The team combines strong accounting fundamentals with an understanding of Equine operations to deliver accurate books, useful reporting, and responsive guidance across complex entities, locations, departments, and horse-related activity.

About the Role

The AFO Consultant - Equine supports the delivery of outsourced accounting and advisory services to Equine clients. Working under the direction of Senior Consultants, Managers, and Directors, this role completes recurring accounting processes, performs assigned month-end close activities, prepares financial reports, and helps maintain accurate records across client entities and operations.

The Consultant applies sound accounting judgment while developing a practical understanding of horse farm, breeding, racing, sales, and ownership activities. This individual also reviews selected work prepared by Associates, provides day-to-day feedback, communicates questions and risks promptly, and contributes to an accurate, efficient, and consistent client experience.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Technical

Definition: Your specialized knowledge and expertise associated with the work you perform for/with clients (note: clients may be internal to Dean Dorton).

Accounting, Close & Reporting

  • Complete assigned month-end close activities and, for selected clients, coordinate the full close process under appropriate review.
  • Prepare financial statements and supporting schedules, including balance sheets, income statements, and statements of cash flows.
  • Prepare and review recurring accounting functions, which may include journal entries, month-end accruals, account reconciliations, payroll activity, fixed assets, sales and use tax, payroll tax returns, and other compliance-related schedules.
  • Review selected work prepared by AFO Associates for accuracy, completeness, and adherence to client and firm procedures; provide clear review comments and escalate significant matters.
  • Perform financial analysis, including budget-to-actual and period-over-period variance analysis, trend analysis, and reports that communicate financial performance and operating results.
  • Support client budgeting, forecasting, cash flow projections, and other forward-looking analyses.
  • Monitor cash balances and cash flow needs, identify potential shortfalls or unusual activity, and communicate findings to the engagement leader.
  • Coordinate the annual Form 1099 process and maintain supporting documentation for assigned clients.
  • Assist with special projects, new-client onboarding, and accounting software implementations or conversions.

Equine Accounting & Client Support

  • Develop an understanding of each client's Equine operations, entity structure, reporting needs, and accounting policies.
  • Maintain accurate coding and classification across horses, farms or locations, departments, entities, and ownership structures in accordance with client-specific requirements.
  • Record and reconcile activity related to horse purchases and sales, breeding and racing operations, boarding and training, farm operations, and other Equine-related revenue and expenses.
  • Prepare schedules and supporting documentation for horse-related assets, fixed assets, inventory, ownership activity, and significant transactions as applicable to the engagement.
  • Reconcile bank, credit card, and operational accounts across single- and multi-entity Equine clients, investigating and resolving differences promptly.
  • Prepare recurring and ad hoc reporting that helps owners and management understand operating results, cash requirements, and activity by entity, location, department, or horse.
  • Coordinate with client contacts and internal team members to obtain missing documentation, resolve coding questions, and keep assigned work moving toward completion.
  • Support Equine client onboarding by documenting processes, establishing charts of accounts and reporting dimensions, and helping configure accounting workflows and technology.

Non-Charge

Definition: The contribution you make to Dean Dorton outside of client work.

  • Complete relevant software training and certifications, which may include BILL, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks, FloQast, and other tools used by the AFO practice.
  • Build Equine industry knowledge through training, research, team discussions, and participation in the AFO Equine industry vertical.
  • Become a dependable resource for selected software, processes, or Equine accounting topics and share knowledge with other team members.
  • Work with a Career Advisor to establish professional goals, pursue development opportunities, and prepare for increased responsibility over time.
  • Participate in internal training, recruiting, marketing, networking, and team-building activities as requested.
  • Contribute ideas that improve AFO templates, workflows, documentation, onboarding, and the consistency of client service.
  • Participate in the Associate Program, when applicable, by supporting networking, training, and relationship-building activities.

Requirements

Experience & Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree, or equivalent experience, in accounting, finance, business, or a related field required.
  • Two to three years of progressive accounting, outsourced accounting, or related financial experience required.
  • Experience with month-end close, general ledger accounting, account reconciliations, journal entries, and financial statement preparation required.
  • Experience serving multiple clients or entities and managing concurrent deadlines preferred.
  • Experience with horse farms, breeding or racing operations, Equine sales companies, agribusiness, or related ownership structures preferred.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, analytical ability, organization, attention to detail, and professional judgment required.

Software & Tools

  • CaseWare
  • Sage Intacct
  • QuickBooks
  • Expensify
  • BILL
  • Yearli
  • BILL Spend & Expense (formerly Divvy)
  • FloQast
  • Adobe
  • Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams)
  • SharePoint and ShareFile

Travel

Travel, including occasional visits to client locations, farms, or firm offices, may be required on an extremely limited basis.

Benefits

The Fun Stuff

Work isn’t all work! We want to make your experience at Dean Dorton a great one. From your health and happiness to your long-term satisfaction, we focus on YOU! A few highlights are listed below:

  • Flexible work schedules and environment
  • Unlimited Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Paid family leave, medical leave, and maternity/paternity leave programs
  • Retirement benefits, including a best-in-class employer match and automatic profit sharing.
  • Telemedicine, mental health resources and wellness program reimbursement

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by team members assigned to this position. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Additionally, responsibilities and duties may vary depending on business needs and individual circumstances.

Dean Dorton is an equal opportunity employer. We’re committed to growing and empowering an inclusive community within Dean Dorton and our industry which is why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of the best and brightest from all backgrounds, experiences and perspectives across the organization. We welcome anyone of any race, religion, color, national origin, political affiliation, pregnancy, ancestry, handicap, medical condition, disability, marital status, age, sexual orientation or gender.

We do not accept unsolicited resumes or candidate submissions from staffing agencies, recruiters, or search firms. Any resumes or candidate information submitted without a current, signed agreement in place will be considered unsolicited, become the property of the company, and will not obligate the company to pay any fees or commissions.

Priorities shift as the work evolves, so we're looking for a versatile engineer who is comfortable moving between a mature codebase and a new one.

You will work in an agile team alongside engineers, designers, a security lead, and help desk staff, and you will see the direct impact of your work on the people who use these systems every day.

Wissen teilen & gemeinsam wachsen: Für dich lebt echte Teamarbeit vom gegenseitigen Austausch. Du bringst Best Practices aus dem Software Engineering ins Data-Team ein und vertiefst gleichzeitig dein eigenes Data- & AI-Wissen, um gemeinsam technologische Herausforderungen zu meistern.

  • Spring, FastAPI, Flask

  • Databricks, Spark, Kafka, Airflow, dbt, BigQuery oder Snowflake

Job Description

This role is designed for an experienced and forward-thinking regulatory project manager who thrives in a fast-paced, innovative environment and can seamlessly integrate strategic thinking with operational execution across all stages of product development, registration, and post-marketing.


As a key member of the Global Regulatory Science team, you will partner strategically with Global Regulatory Leads to shape and execute comprehensive regulatory strategies for the U.S. and ex-U.S. markets. You will lead the development and execution of proactive global regulatory plans that articulate clear milestones, surface risks and opportunities, and support timely, informed regulatory decision-making.


This is a highly visible, cross-functional role requiring strong leadership, agility, and strategic foresight. You will be accountable for driving regulatory excellence by aligning cross-functional stakeholders, managing complex timelines, and anticipating challenges to enable successful delivery of regulatory milestones that support the clients' mission to bring transformative mRNA medicines to patients worldwide.


In close partnership with Global Regulatory Leads, you will also play a key role in facilitating Global Regulatory Subteam (GRST) meetings and subteam forums, ensuring effective meeting structure, clear agendas, documented decisions and actions, timely follow-up, and strong meeting hygiene consistent with project management best practices. This includes helping teams operate with clarity, accountability, and a high-performance mindset through disciplined planning, communication, and execution.

Here’s What You’ll Do

  • Partner strategically with Global Regulatory Leads to shape and execute forward-looking, globally aligned regulatory plans across all stages of development and post-marketing.
  • Translate regulatory strategy into integrated, actionable plans with clear milestones, critical paths, risks, and opportunities to support effective planning and decision-making.
  • Lead the execution of regulatory plans, ensuring alignment between day-to-day operations and broader strategic objectives across global programs.
  • Identify and propose innovative regulatory pathways and planning scenarios that align with global regulatory expectations and business objectives.
  • Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams and senior leadership to drive clarity, alignment, and accountability for regulatory deliverables, timelines, and interdependencies.
  • Facilitate Global Regulatory Subteam (GRST) meetings and other routine and ad hoc project review forums, ensuring meetings are purpose-driven, well-structured, and focused on decision-making, risk mitigation, and regulatory execution.
  • Apply project management best practices for meeting management and hygiene, including developing and distributing agendas in advance, defining objectives and discussion topics, maintaining action logs, documenting key decisions and next steps, tracking follow-up items to closure, and ensuring materials are stored and communicated appropriately.
  • Partner with Global Regulatory Leads and cross-functional stakeholders to maintain effective GRST governance, meeting cadence, stakeholder alignment, and communication flow across global and regional teams.
  • Anticipate and troubleshoot complex regulatory project and operational challenges, implementing scalable solutions that strengthen team effectiveness, process efficiency, and submission readiness.
  • Prepare and deliver strategic dashboards, reports, and scenario plans to senior stakeholders, translating regulatory progress and risks into actionable business insights.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table

  • BA/BS degree in a scientific, engineering, or healthcare discipline required; advanced degree (MS, PharmD, PhD) and/or PMP certification strongly preferred.
  • Minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or related life sciences industry, with at least 5 years in regulatory or regulatory program management.
  • Proven ability to partner on regulatory strategy and lead execution across all stages of product development, including IND/BLA/MAA submissions, global registration, and post-marketing activities.
  • Deep understanding of U.S. regulatory requirements with working knowledge of international (ex-U.S.) regulations and agency expectations.
  • Demonstrated success managing complex regulatory deliverables across cross-functional teams within a matrixed organization, while maintaining alignment to strategic priorities.
  • Hands-on experience with eCTD and a strong command of regulatory documentation, formatting, and submission strategy.
  • Experience supporting global development programs across multiple modalities or therapeutic areas is highly desirable.
  • Exceptional communication and influencing skills, with the ability to synthesize complex regulatory information and translate it into clear recommendations for senior leadership and global stakeholders.
  • Strong judgment and agility in managing competing priorities, resource constraints, and evolving program needs with flexibility and strategic foresight.
  • Demonstrated ability to leverage project management tools and best practices to enhance visibility, efficiency, cross-functional alignment, and meeting effectiveness across GRSTs and project teams.
  • Demonstrated experience facilitating cross-functional team meetings, driving structured agendas, documenting decisions and actions, and maintaining strong meeting hygiene and team accountability in a matrixed environment.
  • Committed to continuous learning and improvement, bringing an innovation mindset to regulatory execution and cross-functional collaboration.

Technical Skill Requirements

  • Expert skills required for Smartsheet and Microsoft Office Suite
  • Expert in creating visuals using PPT generated from timeline integration tools (ie, One Pager, Office Timeline Pro, etc.)
  • Proficient user of Veeva Regulatory Information Management (RIM)

At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.

As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

Upstart’s Unsecured Underwriting Machine Learning team develops and improves the models that inform credit decisions for our unsecured lending products. The team conducts machine learning research, evaluates model performance, and partners closely with Engineering teams to translate promising ideas into scalable model improvements.

As an Applied Scientist, you will research and implement enhancements to Upstart’s core unsecured underwriting model. Your work will directly influence credit decisioning and help the team increase the pace of research while maintaining the rigor, reliability, and responsible oversight required of production underwriting models.

As an Applied Scientist in the Unsecured Underwriting Machine Learning team at Upstart, you will:

  • Research machine learning and statistical approaches that improve the predictive performance of unsecured underwriting models.
  • Design, implement, and evaluate model enhancements using rigorous experimentation and validation methods.
  • Analyze model performance and downstream effects to confirm that proposed changes improve decisioning reliably.
  • Partner with various Engineering teams to support technical reviews, implementation, and deployment.
  • Translate research findings into clear recommendations, documented methodologies, and production-ready solutions.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Graduate degree in mathematics, applied mathematics, statistics, physics, econometrics, operations research, computer science, or a related quantitative field.
  • 2+ years of experience conducting machine learning, statistical modeling, or applied quantitative research in an academic or industry setting.
  • Experience developing and evaluating machine learning or statistical models using Python.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of probability, statistics, and machine learning methods.
  • Experience designing experiments or validation analyses to assess model accuracy, reliability, or predictive performance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD in a quantitative field.
  • Knowledge of supervised learning, model evaluation, and feature engineering techniques.
  • Experience working with large or complex datasets and translating research concepts into implemented solutions.
  • Ability to balance research velocity with analytical rigor, model reliability, and responsible decision-making.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain technical concepts and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and stakeholders from diverse backgrounds.

Position location This role is available in the following locations: Remote

The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S or Canada (outside of Quebec) but are expected to spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites and in-person meetings. The onsite cadence varies depending on the team and role; most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2-4 consecutive days at a time.

Meet Instinct 👋

Instinct Science is at the forefront of veterinary innovation, comprised of world-class tools that have served our industry for decades: easy-to-use veterinary practice software (Instinct EMR), an essential resource for expanding your knowledge and skills (Clinician's Brief), clinical and pharmaceutical decision support (Standards of Care & Plumb's), and an AI scribing platform (ScribbleVet). At Instinct Science, we believe in leading with compassion. Our team, our customers, and their patients and clients are the foundation of everything we do. Our culture is guided by our U.C.A.R.E. values: We move fast because our mission matters, we put customers at the center of every decision, and we treat each other with kindness and high standards.

A Sneak Peek of Your Role 🔭

This is a fully remote role.

Instinct Science builds an ecosystem of AI-powered and clinical software products used across veterinary medicine including ScribbleVet (AI documentation), Instinct EMR, Clinician's Brief, Standards of Care, and Plumb's. We're hiring an Account Executive to sell across that full suite.

This is not a single-product, single-segment role. Expect to move between fast-cycle SMB opportunities and Mid-Market and Enterprise deals where you're navigating multiple stakeholders, longer evaluation cycles, and higher ACVs.

For an SMB AE ready to make the jump into more complex selling, this role is built as a launchpad: you get the volume and reps to keep your number predictable, the suite to maximize ACV per deal, and the deal complexity that builds careers.

What You'll Do 🛠️

  • Own and convert a high volume of inbound leads from end users and decision-makers across customer segments
  • Run tailored product demos that connect each product's features to the specific workflow challenges a prospect faces
  • Drive trial-to-paid conversion through consistent, consultative follow-up - surfacing friction and helping champions build internal momentum
  • Cross-sell and bundle across the Instinct suite (ScribbleVet, EMR, Clinician's Brief, Treatment Plans, Standards of Care, Plumb's) to deliver more value per account
  • Work Mid-Market and Enterprise opportunities alongside your SMB pipeline - multi-stakeholder deals, longer cycles, and larger contracts
  • Apply a structured deal framework (MEDDIC, SPICED, or equivalent) and a value-based selling approach to qualify, advance, and close
  • Manage a fast pipeline with discipline: clean CRM hygiene, reliable forecasting, and accurate next steps

    • Working fluency in a structured deal framework (MEDDIC, SPICED, MEDDPICC, or similar) and value-based selling
    • Strong product demonstration skills with the ability to adapt your pitch to different audience types (individual end users vs. team leads vs. owners/operators)
    • A consultative, low-pressure style that builds trust quickly and helps prospects make confident decisions
    • Comfort managing a high volume of active deals simultaneously alongside a smaller number of more complex, larger-ACV opportunities
    • Proficiency with CRM tools (HubSpot preferred) and a data-driven approach to pipeline management
    • Excellent written and verbal communication
    • Self-directed, accountable, and biased toward action
  • Preferred:
    • Experience selling AI-powered products or in a product-led growth motion where trial/freemium conversion is core to the sales cycle

Five years minimum of current and proven end-to-end security solutions sales experience. You embody our values: Hunger, Heart, and Harmony.

About Bridgespan

The Bridgespan Group is a leading nonprofit consulting organization serving ambitious nonprofit leaders, philanthropists, and impact investors in North America, Asia, and Africa. We work with social change organizations, philanthropies, impact investors, and collaborative initiatives to help them achieve greater social impact.

We value diversity, passion, respect, candor, and impact while working toward societies characterized by equity and justice. We are committed to building a diverse team and leadership at all levels, developing a truly inclusive culture, and integrating equity into our work.

We are seeking an experienced Director, Business Applications to lead the strategy, delivery, operation, and continued development of the applications that support Bridgespan's core business processes.

Who you are

  • You are an experienced business applications leader who can connect organizational strategy, business processes, and technology decisions.
  • You have led multidisciplinary teams that include product managers or business systems analysts, system administrators, and engineers. You set clear direction while giving specialists the context and accountability they need to deliver.
  • You understand that business applications require both a strong roadmap and disciplined day-to-day operation. You are comfortable moving between executive decisions, business requirements, technical architecture, delivery risks, release planning, and support issues.
  • You build trusted partnerships with functional leaders and can translate needs from HR, Finance, Marketing, and other teams into practical system priorities and investment choices.
  • You have managed external implementation and support partners and can determine when work should remain with a managed service provider and when bringing capabilities in-house would improve service, control, or cost.
  • You are motivated by Bridgespan's mission and want to strengthen the systems that enable our staff to serve social sector leaders effectively.

What you will do

Reporting to the Chief Information and Technology Officer, the Director, Business Applications will be accountable for the strategy, roadmap, delivery, administration, reliability, and ongoing improvement of Bridgespan's enterprise business applications. The initial portfolio includes the organization's Microsoft Dynamics (CRM) and Workday (ERP) systems. The portfolio may expand to include other systems that support organization-wide business processes.

The Director will lead a multidisciplinary team of product managers or business systems analysts , system administrators, and engineers. The role combines the product and engineering leadership responsibilities needed to translate business priorities into a coherent roadmap, execute that roadmap, and operate the resulting systems well. The Director will also oversee external partners, including the managed service provider that currently supports the ERP system, and will recommend the right long-term balance of internal and external capabilities.

Success in this role will be measured by the business value, reliability, adoption, security, and cost-effectiveness of Bridgespan’s enterprise business applications; the clarity and execution of the roadmap; the quality of partnerships with business owners; and the strength and scalability of the enterprise systems team.

Key responsibilities

  • Business systems strategy and roadmapSet the vision and multi-year roadmap and investment plan for CRM, ERP, and future business applications. Align priorities with Bridgespan's strategy, business value, system health, risk, capacity, and total cost of ownership. Own budget planning, forecasting, licensing strategy, contract economics, and benefits realization, and communicate the financial implications of system choices to senior leaders.
  • Portfolio prioritization and governanceEstablish a clear process for evaluating requests, resolving tradeoffs, sequencing work, and communicating decisions. Ensure that roadmap commitments reflect available business, technical, and change-management capacity.
  • Business partnership and requirementsPartner with HR, Finance, Marketing, and other business owners to understand processes, identify problems and opportunities, define requirements, and establish shared ownership for decisions, data, adoption, and outcomes.
  • System delivery and lifecycle managementLead work from discovery and solution design through configuration, development, testing, release, adoption, and post-launch support. Coordinate dependencies across systems and keep complex initiatives on scope, schedule, and budget. Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Cybersecurity, and Infrastructure teams on solution & data architecture, system integrations, cybersecurity and infrastructure & operations governance, standards, processes, policies and guidelines.
  • Engineering, configurations, and extensionsDirect the development and configuration of business applications and related extensions. Set expectations for architecture, development practices, testing, documentation, release management, data flow, maintainability, and technical quality.
  • System administration and operational excellenceEnsure effective administration, access management, monitoring, issue resolution, vendor coordination, and user support. Define service expectations and operating practices that keep systems secure, reliable, usable, and well documented.
  • Vendor and managed services oversightOwn relationships with implementation partners, software vendors, and managed service providers. Set performance expectations, manage contracts and costs, and hold partners accountable for service quality and delivery. Regularly assess whether capabilities should remain outsourced or move in-house based on service, risk, capacity, and cost.
  • Data governance and quality Partner with the data governance function, data leaders, cybersecurity, and technology teams to help establish data definitions, lineage, quality standards, retention practices, and controls for data managed by the business applications within the scope of responsibility. Ensure that integrations and reporting use trusted data and that data issues are identified, prioritized, and resolved.
  • Team leadershipLead, coach, and develop a multidisciplinary business systems team. Clarify roles and decision rights, strengthen collaboration across product, administration, and engineering, and build the capabilities needed for the future business applications portfolio.
  • Risk, security, and business continuityWork with security, data, infrastructure, and business partners to identify and manage risks related to access, integrations, data handling, releases, vendor dependencies, system resilience, and continuity of critical business processes.
  • Adoption, performance, and continuous improvementUse service data, system metrics, user feedback, and business outcomes to evaluate performance and adoption. Lead communication, training, and process changes needed to realize value from technology investments and improve them over time.

The ideal candidate should have

Required qualifications

  • 10 or more years of experience in business applications/ systems, product management, software delivery, or a related technology field.
  • At least five years of experience leading people and multidisciplinary teams, including professionals working in product or business analysis, system administration, and engineering.Experience owning the strategy, roadmap, delivery, and operation of MS Dynamics CRM, Workday ERP, HRIS, finance, or comparable business applications.
  • Experience leading complex system implementations, major enhancements, integrations, and ongoing lifecycle management.
  • Working knowledge of application architecture, APIs and integrations, data flows, software development practices, testing, release management, security, and support operations.
  • Experience implementing or improving data governance, data quality, ownership, controls, and reporting practices across business applications and integrations.
  • Experience managing software vendors, implementation partners, or managed service providers, including performance, contracts, costs, and sourcing decisions.
  • Strong portfolio management and prioritization skills, including the ability to evaluate business value, risk, dependencies, capacity, and total cost of ownership.
  • A record of building effective partnerships with senior leaders, functional owners, and technical teams and translating business needs into clear decisions and executable plans.
  • Experience collaborating with colleagues across multiple geographies
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical choices, delivery risks, and tradeoffs to non-technical audiences.
  • Sound judgment, accountability, and the ability to bring structure to ambiguous and changing situations.
  • Passion for Bridgespan's mission and a demonstrated commitment to racial equity, diversity, and inclusion.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with marketing technology systems and the integration of marketing, CRM, and enterprise data.
  • Experience evaluating or executing a transition between outsourced and in-house system administration or engineering capabilities.
  • Experience supporting digital transformation in a consulting, professional services, nonprofit, or other mission-driven organization.
  • Familiarity with delivery and documentation tools such as Jira and Confluence.

Remote Work Eligibility

This is a remote position. However, due to employment authorization requirements, we can only employ individuals who reside in states where we are currently authorized to operate.

Eligible U.S. states: Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, North Carolina, North Dakota, Virginia, West Virginia, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington, D.C.

About Improvado

Improvado is an AI-powered marketing data platform built for mid-market and enterprise teams. We help companies automate complex marketing data workflows, unify data at scale, and surface insights through BI and AI. Brands like Genentech, T-Mobile, Activision, and H&R Block rely on us to simplify analytics and improve marketing performance.

We’re a fast-growing Series A startup backed by $34M in funding and driven by a team that moves fast, stays curious, and cares about high-quality execution.

About the role

Improvado is a marketing data platform for enterprise brands and agencies. You will own how our revenue runs and how it is measured. That covers Salesforce and the GTM tools, the path from signed contract to paid invoice, the revenue data model, and the reports leadership decides from. You work closely with the analytics team: you don’t have to build the data models yourself, but you must read them, spot what is wrong and say what to change. You work through AI agents daily, doing the work of a bigger team.

What you will do

Salesforce and GTM stack

  • Own Salesforce configuration, release process and user access, plus the integrations around it (Gong, Clay, Lemlist, enrichment, e-signature, lead routing).
  • Keep CRM data clean with guardrails that block mistakes. Manage licences and vendor renewals.
  • Maintain the Salesforce manual and RevOps SOPs, and train new hires.

Contract to cash

  • Own ARR and bookings logic (new, upsell, downsell, churn, renewals) and keep agreement, opportunity, and invoice consistent.
  • Run the closed-deals and billing check with Finance. Fix errors at the source and add a control so they don’t repeat.
  • Audit invoices, track and chase unpaid ones, and prepare quarterly commission and quota reports.

Revenue analytics and data model

  • Own the quarterly sales analytics pack, the CRO report, the forecast and pipeline coverage (including CS renewal inputs).
  • Track funnel conversion, explain why deals move, stall or slip, and keep attribution correct with Marketing.
  • Query ClickHouse daily, trace any number to its source, and write specs for model changes. Give each metric one documented definition and add data quality checks.
  • Build leadership dashboards, retire unused ones, and end every analysis with a recommendation, a number and an owner.

AI and automation

  • Use coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) for queries, scripts and Salesforce automation, and always verify their output.
  • Automate manual work (invoice and payment checks, CRM hygiene, deal-risk alerts, call analysis) and measure hours saved and errors avoided.

Ownership

  • Be the single RevOps contact for Sales, CS, Marketing, Finance and Product. Turn each request into a task with an owner, date and success metric.

Requirements

  • 4-6+ years in RevOps, Sales Ops or GTM systems in B2B SaaS, with hands-on admin of a live Salesforce org.
  • Strong SQL and comfort in a modeled warehouse (layers, lineage, one definition per metric). dbt is a plus.
  • Deep knowledge of the B2B SaaS revenue cycle: funnel, pipeline, forecast, ARR, churn, renewals.
  • Experience running the money side: contracts, invoicing, collections, kept in sync with the CRM.
  • Proof you build with AI agents: something you shipped that others use.
  • Fluent English and clear written updates without being asked.

Nice to have

  • Salesforce Administrator or Advanced Administrator certification.
  • ClickHouse or another columnar warehouse, and any BI tool.
  • Salesforce development (Apex, triggers, API).
  • Gong, Clay, Lemlist, or workflow automation tools.
  • Billing, CPQ, or accounting systems.
  • HubSpot to Salesforce migration.
  • Attribution or CS health score data.
  • Martech or analytics company background.

What We Offer

  • Remote-first environment
  • Strong product/market fit: marketing data product for US-based enterprises
  • 20 working days of PTO per year
  • US holidays and additional days off
  • Professional development reimbursement

Pas de stage passé derrière un écran à regarder les autres vendre : tu seras rapidement sur le terrain.

Qui cherchons-nous ?

Pas forcément quelqu’un qui connaît déjà parfaitement la pharmacie.

On cherche surtout quelqu’un qui :

  • Aime vendre et convaincre

  • N’a pas peur de pousser une porte et de prospecter

  • Aime rencontrer des clients

  • Est autonome et organisé

  • A envie d’apprendre vite

  • Aime avoir des objectifs et les dépasser

  • A envie de prendre des responsabilités

Tu es en école de commerce, vente, business development, pharmacie ou formation équivalente.

Une première expérience commerciale est appréciée. Ton état d’esprit et ton potentiel feront surtout la différence.

Pourquoi Alpine ?

Alpine est une entreprise internationale présente dans plus de 50 pays, partenaire de grandes salles de concert

européennes et présente au cœur de la Formule 1.

Notre mission : permettre à chacun de profiter pleinement de chaque expérience tout en protégeant son audition. En

concert, sur un circuit, en voyage, dans l’eau ou simplement pour mieux dormir.

En France, nous sommes encore une petite équipe avec de grosses ambitions.

Tu travailleras au contact direct de l’équipe France, avec beaucoup d’autonomie et la possibilité de voir concrètement l’impact de ton travail.

LOCALISATION Sud-Est · Départements 34 / 30 / 13 / 83 / 06 (télétravail)

DURÉE 6 mois

CONTRAT Stage conventionné

DÉMARRAGE Dès que possible

Envie d’avoir ton propre secteur plutôt que d’observer depuis le siège ? Rejoins-nous.

Requirements

Sud-Est region · 34 / 30 / 13 / 83 / 06 · 6 months · Fully remote

Alpine Hearing Protection is accelerating its growth in France and is looking for a Pharmacy Business Developer to develop the South-East of France (departments 34 / 30 / 13 / 83 / 06).

Our ambition is clear: to make Alpine a leading hearing protection brand in French pharmacies.

And to make that happen, we need people in the field.

Your playground

Over 6 months, you will progressively take ownership of your own territory.

  • Prospect and open new pharmacy accounts

  • Meet pharmacists and their teams

  • Develop existing Alpine pharmacy customers

  • Train pharmacy teams on our products and consumer needs

  • Improve our visibility at point of sale

  • Generate reorders

  • Identify new business opportunities across your territory

You will have real business objectives: new customers, revenue, reorders, training and in-store execution.

This is not an internship spent behind a screen watching others sell: you will quickly be out in the field.

Who are we looking for?

You do not need to already know the pharmacy market inside out.

We are mainly looking for someone who:

  • Enjoys selling and convincing

  • Is not afraid to knock on doors and prospect

  • Enjoys meeting customers

  • Is autonomous and organised

  • Wants to learn fast

  • Likes having targets and exceeding them

  • Wants to take responsibility

You are studying business, sales, business development, pharmacy or an equivalent field.

Previous sales experience is appreciated. Your mindset and potential will make the real difference.

Why Alpine?

Alpine is an international company present in more than 50 countries, partnering with major European concert venues and active at the heart of Formula 1.

Our mission is to help people fully enjoy every experience while protecting their hearing. At a concert, on a racetrack, while travelling, in the water, or simply while getting a better night’s sleep.

In France, we are still a small team with big ambitions.

You will work directly with the French team, with a high level of autonomy and the opportunity to see the concrete impact of your work.

LOCATION South-East France · Departments 34 / 30 / 13 / 83 / 06 (remote)

DURATION 6 months

CONTRACT Internship agreement required

START DATE As soon as possible

Want your own territory instead of watching from the sidelines? Join us.

jobs.excerpt: Who we are We’re a global, midsize CRO that pushes boundaries, innovates and invents because the path to a cure for the world’s most persistent diseases is not paved by those who play it safe.
jobs.description:
Who we are

We’re a global, midsize CRO that pushes boundaries, innovates and invents because the path to a cure for the world’s most persistent diseases is not paved by those who play it safe. It is built by those who take pioneering, creative approaches and implement them with quality and excellence.

We are Worldwide Clinical Trials, and we are a global team of over 3,500+ experts, bright thinkers, dreamers and doers and, together, we are changing the way the world experiences CROs – in the best possible way.

Our mission is to work with passion and purpose every day to improve lives and we are looking for others who value this same pursuit.

Why Worldwide

We believe everyone plays an important role in making a world of difference for patients and their caregivers. From our hands-on, accessible leaders, to our cohesive and supportive teams, we are committed to enabling professionals from all backgrounds and experiences to succeed. We prioritize cultivating a diverse and inclusive environment that continues to promote collaboration and creativity. We are proud to be a workplace where people thrive by being themselves and are inspired to do their best work every day. Join us!

What Clinical Operations does at Worldwide

At Worldwide Clinical Trials, we invite you to embark on a rewarding journey within Clinical Operations, where your contributions will leave a profound impact on the lives of patients.

As a Clinical Research Associate (CRA) at Worldwide, you will find yourself working alongside brilliant minds across diverse therapeutic areas, including Cardiovascular, Metabolic, Neuroscience, Oncology, and Rare Diseases. Collaboration with top-tier colleagues from various backgrounds and specialties is not just encouraged; it's ingrained in our culture. Our commitment to advancing clinical research is nurtured within a supportive and team-oriented environment. In a CRA role, you'll receive extensive support through regulatory submissions, TMF management, and in-house CRAs for projects with heavy site management needs.

Through regular touchpoints and coaching conversations with your Line Manager, we ensure that your professional development remains a top priority. We offer a clear career path and development that can lead to Clinical Trial Manager roles. We take pride in our accessible Executive Leadership team, who are equally committed to advancing science and surmounting obstacles to make a difference in the lives of patients around the world.

We offer an unparalleled experience, where you can drive remarkable scientific breakthroughs and be at the very core of every successful clinical trial. Experience a world of difference with us at Worldwide!

What you will do

  • Responsible for managing the research activities at sites participating in Worldwide’s clinical research projects

  • Typically involved in all stages of the clinical study, including identifying potential sites to participate in the research effort, performing various study start-up activities such as working with sites to collect appropriate regulatory documents and supporting the negotiation of contracts and budgets, training the sites to collect data properly and report any potential safety-related events, managing the site's activities during study maintenance, and closing down research activities at the sites once the study has concluded

  • Conduct study initiation visits (SIVs)

  • While most of the site management efforts will be performed remotely, you will be required to ensure compliance with obtaining informed consent, reporting potential safety-related events, and adhering to all applicable regulatory requirements

What you will bring to the role

  • Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills in English

  • Superior organizational skills with attention to detail

  • Ability to work with little or no supervision

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, CTMS, and EDC Systems

Your experience

  • 5+ years of experience as a Clinical Research Associate

  • 4-year university degree OR Nursing Degree

  • Experience in CNS is required, Rare Disease is preferred

  • Candidates must reside in the Southeastern United States

  • Willingness to travel regionally required

At Worldwide Clinical Trials, we are committed to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace by providing transparent compensation.

United States of America - $97,000.00 - $193,000.00

Salary information will be discussed during the interview process, and we encourage candidates to inquire about compensation at any stage.

We love knowing that someone is going to have a better life because of the work we do.

jobs.excerpt: Who Are We? Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other.
jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That’s the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Job Category

Claim

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$132,800.00 - $219,100.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Investigate, evaluate, reserve, negotiate and resolve the company's most severe and/or complex claims, in multiple jurisdictions, in accordance with Best Practices. Provide quality claim handling and superior customer service on assigned claims, while engaging in indemnity & expense management. Promptly manage claims by completing essential functions including contacts, investigation, damages development, evaluation, reserving, litigation management, negotiating and resolution. Provides consulting and training and serves as an expert technical resource to other claim professionals, business partners, customers, and other stakeholders as appropriate or required. This may include a specific assignment as a severity management resource to one or more field offices.

What Will You Do?

  • CLAIM HANDLING:
  • Directly handle the Company's most severe and complex claims when Travelers has coverage of $2 million or greater and file exposure is greater than $2 million.
  • Provide quality customer service and ensure file quality timely coverage analysis and communication with insured based on application of policy information to facts or allegations of each case.
  • Directly investigate each claim through prompt and strategically-appropriate contact with appropriate parties such as policyholders, accounts, claimants, law enforcement agencies, witnesses, agents, medical providers and technical experts to determine the extent of liability, damages, and contribution potential.
  • Interview witnesses and stakeholders; take necessary statements, as strategically appropriate.
  • Complete outside investigation as needed per case specifics.
  • Actively engage in the identification, selection and direction of appropriate internal and./or external resources for specific activities required to effectively evaluate claims, such as Subro, Risk Control, nurse consultants and fire or fraud investigators and other experts.
  • Verify the nature and extent of injury or property damage by obtaining and reviewing appropriate records and damages documentation.
  • Utilize diary management system to ensure that all claims are handled timely.
  • At required time intervals, evaluate liability & damages exposure.
  • Establish and maintain proper indemnity & expense reserves.
  • Share experience and deep knowledge of creative resolution techniques to improve the claim results of others.
  • Apply the Company's claim quality management protocols, Best Practices and metrics to all claims; document the rationale for any departure from applicable protocols and metrics.
  • Develop and employ creative resolution strategies.
  • Effectively and efficiently manage both allocated and unallocated loss adjustment expenses
  • Evaluate all claims for recovery potential; directly handle recovery efforts and/or engage and direct Company resources for recovery efforts.
  • Responsible for prompt and proper disposition of all claims within delegated authority. Negotiate disposition of claims with insureds and claimants or their legal representatives.
  • Ensure that the right resources are being applied to each claim to achieve the best result at the most optimal cost.
  • LEADERSHIP:
  • Actively provide mentoring and coaching to less experienced claim professionals to increase the technical expertise and improve bench strength.
  • Field Severity Support: Some Complex Claim Specialists may be responsible for all or some of the following:
  • Collaborate with field severity units in the management and evaluation of some of the Company's severe and complex liability claims by providing claim handling guidance, recommendations and strategies to Field Product Line Managers, Unit Managers, and Major Case Specialists, for timely, cost effective resolution of liability major cases.
  • Provide mentoring or training as request by field severity management.
  • COMMUNICATION/INFLUENCE:
  • Consult with Manager on use of Claim Coverage Counsel as needed.
  • Provide guidance to underwriting business partners with res accuracy and adequacy of, and potential future changes to, loss reserves on assigned claims.
  • Recommend appropriate cases for discussion at roundtable.
  • Attend and or present at roundtables/authority discussions for collaboration of technical expertise resulting in improved payout on indemnity and expense.
  • Update appropriate parties as needed, providing new facts as they become available, and their impact upon the liability analysis and settlement options.
  • Represent the company as a technical resource, attend legal proceedings as needed, act within established professional guidelines as well as applicable state laws
  • Obtain and evaluate current information regarding trends in the law; digest and communicate this information to other Company departments and divisions to assist in underwriting and management decisions.
  • Assist underwriting business partners in marketing and account-contact.
  • Actively participate in the coverage, liability and damages analysis and development of creative resolution strategy for severity cases handled in the field.
  • Assist in the recognition of available defenses to contain loss payout and setting of appropriate reserves.
  • Regularly and actively participate in field severity roundtables to share expertise and recommendations in all aspects of severe claim management.
  • Collaborate with the severity unit in compliance with company claim policies, procedures, practices and standards for the handling of cases that meet the Critical Claim referral guidelines.
  • OTHER ACCOUNTABILITIES:
  • Apply expert litigation management through the selection of counsel, evaluation and direction of claim and litigation strategy.
  • Recognize and implement alternate means of resolution.
  • Manages litigated claims. Develop litigation plan with staff or panel counsel, including discovery and legal expenses, to assure effective resolution and to satisfy our customers.
  • Track and control legal expenses to assure cost-effective resolution.
  • Develop and employ innovative techniques to manage expense and outcome when independent counsel is engaged.
  • Attend depositions, mediations, arbitrations, pre-trials, trials and all other legal proceedings, as needed.
  • Closely monitor independent counsel to ensure quality product.
  • Actively participate in periodic file quality reviews.
  • Appropriately deal with information that is considered personal and confidential.
  • Fulfill specific service commitments made to certain accounts, as outlined in Special Account Communication (SAC) instructions, and inquiries from agents and brokers.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • College degree preferred or equivalent business experience.
  • 5-10 years experience handling serious injury and complex liability claims preferred (casualty claim operations environment determining coverage, liability, investigation, research, evaluation, negotiation and settlement).
  • Position requires a proficiency in oral and written communications.
  • Advanced communications skills are required to understand, interpret and convey highly technical information in simple terms to others.
  • Thorough understanding of product lines, objectives of claim management, and legal theory issues involving claim resolution.
  • Familiarity with commercial lines/personal lines products, policy language, exclusions, ISO forms, effective claims handling practices.
  • Extensive experience handling large exposure and/or complex liability claims.
  • Familiarity with commercial lines products, policy language, exclusions, ISO forms, effective claims handling practices.
  • Thorough understanding of the litigation process, relevant case and statutory law.
  • Ability to recognize, analyze and advise on complex coverage, liability and damage issues.
  • Expert written and verbal communication skills to understand, synthesize, interpret and convey complex data.
  • Create and manage positive working relationships with business and marketing partners.
  • Ability to analyze and effectively respond to human resource issues.
  • Utilize technology as a strategic tool.
  • Ability to make independent decisions up to $1,000,000 without involvement of supervisor.
  • Competencies:
  • Leading the Business - Drive Results.
  • Leads Change - Executes Business Strategy.
  • Leading Others - Attract Top Talent, Maximize Individual Performance, Holds Others Accountable, Aligns Rewards, Creates and Sustains a Dynamic Workplace.
  • Leading Self-Emotional Intelligence - Demonstrates Self-Awareness, Initiative and accountability, Applies Critical Thinking, Communications Effectively & Influences Others, Exhibits Courage, Conviction & Credibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Degree or GED.
  • 5 years bodily injury litigation claim handling experience or 10 years litigation experience.
  • In order to perform the essential job functions of this job, acquisition and maintenance of Insurance License(s) may be required to comply with state and Travelers requirements.
  • Generally, license(s) are required to be obtained within three months of starting the job.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members – including spouses, domestic partners, and children – are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

  • Create schedules and support internal reporting packages for finance and accounting leadership, ensuring accuracy, clarity and adherence to timelines

  • Ensure compliance with internal controls, accounting policies, and procedures to support audit readiness and risk mitigation

  • Support internal and external audits by providing timely documentation and clear explanations to meet audit deadlines and requirements

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams and identify process improvement opportunities, including automation initiatives to enhance efficiency and reporting accuracy

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance or Accounting

  • 4-6 years of accounting experience in public accounting or industry (level to be determined based on experience)

  • Strong knowledge of US GAAP, accounting principles, internal controls, and strong financial literacy

  • Experience with general ledger and other financial systems and preparation of account reconciliations and analysis

  • OracleEPM/Hyperion or similar financial data tool experience is a plus

  • Familiarity with ERP systems (e.g., Workday, Oracle, SAP, PeopleSoft)

  • Specialized Knowledge: Familiarity with SOX compliance or other regulatory frameworks

  • Soft Skills: Strong analytical thinking, communication, and ability to work cross-functionally

  • Process Improvement: Exposure to automation or process optimization initiatives

YOUR LIFE AND CAREER AT SAKS GLOBAL:

  • Opportunity to work in a dynamic fast paced environment at a company experiencing growth and transformation

  • Exposure to rewarding career advancement opportunities across the largest multi-brand luxury retailer from retail to distribution, to digital or corporate

The Opportunity:

The Senior Director of Global Governance, Assurance & Strategy for Environmental, Health, Safety, Security, and Sustainability (EHS3) is responsible for defining and executing the long-term strategy for the global EHS3 function. The role provides enterprise leadership across Governance & Assurance, Environmental Compliance, Occupational Health & Safety, Security, Sustainability, Enterprise Risk Management, and Operational Excellence, ensuring alignment with business objectives, regulatory requirements, and operational priorities.

Leading a global organization through subordinate Directors, Senior Managers, and regional leaders, this position is accountable for the performance and integration of multiple EHS3 functions. The role oversees workforce planning, organizational design, resource allocation, and strategic execution while driving enterprise standards, governance frameworks, and transformational initiatives that strengthen operational performance, risk management, compliance, and business continuity.

As a member of the senior leadership team, the Senior Director partners with executive leaders to establish enterprise priorities, guide strategic investments, and shape long-range organizational plans. The position serves as a key authority on EHS3 strategy and performance, making decisions that significantly impact corporate objectives, operational resilience, regulatory exposure, sustainability outcomes, and organizational reputation worldwide.

How you will thrive and create an impact


EHS Governance:

  • Establish and maintain the enterprise EHS management system, standards, processes, and governance framework.
  • Establish consistent, standardized, and scalable EHS processes across sites and business units.
  • Eliminate unnecessary process complexity, duplication, waste, and administrative burden.
  • Establish clear process ownership, accountability, performance expectations, and escalation pathways.
  • Ensure EHS processes deliver both risk reduction and operational value.

Regulatory & Compliance Assurance:

  • Identify opportunities for process optimization using performance data, employee feedback, audits, incidents, observations, and benchmarking.
  • Stay current on evolving global EHS regulations and legislation, ensuring that the organization remains compliant with all local, national, and international regulations.
  • Act as the subject matter expert on EHS regulations and compliance requirements, providing guidance and support to senior leadership and operational teams.
  • Manage relationships with regulatory bodies, ensuring timely communication, compliance reporting, and responses to regulatory inquiries.
  • Establish a proactive framework for EHS regulatory compliance.
  • Oversee assessments, audits, inspections, and corrective-action programs.

Process Performance & Standardization:

  • Establish process-performance measures for critical EHS processes.
  • Identify process variation, inefficiencies, and opportunities to improve process capability.
  • Benchmark processes across sites to identify performance gaps and opportunities.
  • Develop enterprise standards while allowing appropriate flexibility for site-specific risks and regulatory requirements.
  • Develop and maintain key performance indicators (KPIs) and reporting systems to monitor EHS compliance performance globally.

Continuous Improvement & Innovation:

  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives in the EHS process compliance domain, leveraging technology and industry innovations to drive efficiencies and enhance compliance management systems.
  • Implement and manage global EHS audit programs, corrective action tracking, and follow-up to ensure that audit findings are addressed promptly.
  • Translate lessons learned from incidents and near misses into enterprise improvement initiatives.
  • Establish an enterprise approach for identifying and managing high-risk and Serious Injury/Fatality (SIF) exposures.

Incident Management & Organizational Learning

  • Establish governance for serious and high-potential incident investigations.
  • Ensure investigations identify systemic process and organizational causes.
  • Convert recurring incident trends into Continuous Improvement initiatives.
  • Establish sustainable corrective actions and verify their effectiveness.
  • Share lessons learned and successful solutions across the organization.
  • Identify opportunities to redesign processes to prevent recurrence.

Data, Analytics & Digital Transformation

  • Establish EHS data governance and performance standards.
  • Use data analytics to identify process inefficiencies, variation, and emerging risks.
  • Develop dashboards connecting EHS performance with operational performance.
  • Identify opportunities to automate manual EHS processes.
  • Leverage digital tools to improve workflow, action management, audits, training, and reporting.
  • Establish methods for measuring the effectiveness and sustainability of improvement programs.

Enterprise EHS3 Strategy & Organizational Leadership

  • Establish and continuously evolve the global EHS3 strategic plan, ensuring alignment with corporate business strategy and long-term growth objectives.
  • Direct multiple global EHS3 functional organizations through a tiered leadership structure consisting of Directors, Senior Managers, and functional leaders.
  • Maintain accountability for the performance, effectiveness, and integration of Environmental, Health & Safety, Security, Sustainability, Governance & Assurance, and Risk Management functions.
  • Lead organizational design decisions, succession planning, workforce strategy, and talent development across the global EHS3 organization.
  • Establish enterprise performance objectives and strategic priorities for all EHS3 functional disciplines.
  • Determine long-range organizational capabilities required to support future business expansion, acquisitions, and operational transformation.

Executive Leadership & Enterprise Influence

  • Serve as the principal advisor to executive leadership on EHS3 risk, governance, compliance, sustainability, and security matters.
  • Partner regularly with Executive Leadership Team members to establish company-wide policies, operational priorities, and strategic initiatives.
  • Influence enterprise business decisions where EHS3 performance, risk management, sustainability goals, or regulatory exposure could materially impact organizational outcomes.
  • Represent the company with key regulators, industry associations, board-level committees, investors, and external stakeholders on strategic EHS3 matters.

Financial, Resource & Workforce Accountability

  • Own and manage a significant global EHS3 operating budget, including annual planning, investment prioritization, and resource allocation.
  • Establish enterprise workforce plans, organizational staffing strategies, and capability-building initiatives across all EHS3 functions.
  • Direct capital planning and investment decisions related to EHS3 systems, technologies, compliance programs, facilities, and strategic initiatives.
  • Ensure effective allocation of resources across regions, business units, and functional disciplines to achieve enterprise objectives.
  • Maintain accountability for achieving business results through responsible stewardship of financial, technology, and human capital resources.

Multi-Functional Governance & Performance Management

  • Direct the integration of environmental compliance, occupational safety, security, sustainability, governance, assurance, and enterprise risk management programs into a unified global operating model.
  • Establish enterprise-wide priorities, standards, and performance expectations across all EHS3 disciplines.
  • Resolve competing business priorities and allocate resources across multiple functional areas to optimize enterprise outcomes.
  • Lead cross-functional strategic initiatives with broad organizational impact and long-term business consequences.

What we're looking for


Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Safety Engineering, Occupational Health, or related field (master’s or advanced degree preferred).

Experience:

  • Minimum 15+ years of progressive global leadership experience within Environmental, Health & Safety, Security, Sustainability, Governance, Risk, or Compliance functions.
  • Minimum 10 years leading large, multi-functional organizations through subordinate Directors and senior leaders.
  • Demonstrated success developing enterprise strategy, managing significant global budgets, and leading large-scale organizational transformation initiatives.
  • Proven experience influencing executive leadership and driving strategic decisions with enterprise-wide impact.
